# Canal Recall — what is built

**Keyboard-ride unstuck; follow-ups to street following (2026-10-29).**
- `keyboard-ride.spec.ts` failed 7 of 8 core rides on main (since before the
  street-follow change, same rides at cbcace987). Cause, in the game and the
  spec: a *silent pass* (a name the question budget declines, no card, bike
  free) sets `quizPromptName`. The previous answer's hold timer read that as
  a new question and never hid the answered card, so it stayed up until the
  rider left the street; the spec, also reading it as a question, released
  the keys and waited, so the rider never left. `answerHoldMayHide`
  (silentPass.ts, unit-tested) closes the card under a silent pass; the spec
  ignores silent passes. 8/8 pass.
- `mobile-overlays` "absolute mode" asserted a north-up map; chase (default
  since 10-22) holds the starting bearing. It now asserts what absolute mode
  promises: the map holds still and the stick's right is screen-right.
- Boats: the grass push eased the bow toward the nearest centreline *point*
  (sideways) — now along the water. `test:street-follow` pins Prinsengracht ×
  Leidsegracht both ways; it caught a queued left spent on the Prinsengracht's
  own 35° bend. A choice on the way underfoot is never a turn, and a gentle
  split between two ways of one name is not a fork.
- A queued turn now shows a pulsing chevron on the map at the opening it will
  take (no label: the street may be the question).

**Touch devices spread the shader warm-up (2026-10-29, #106, Sentry
CANAL-RECALL-7/-J/-N).** A Firefox Mobile 159 / Android 17 phone lost its WebGL
context 7.8 s in, got it back, and then its GPU died at 11.3 s while compiling
shaders (2 -> 22 programs). The rider never pressed Start: the guest briefing
reproduces the Sentry probe exactly (`scripts/gpu-startup-timeline.mjs`).
Touch classification and memory were fine. The cause was `OwnGround.precompile()`
linking about 21 three.js programs in one task, on top of MapLibre's ~16, and again
after every restore. `rendererShared/compileBudget.ts` lets a coarse-pointer
device link at most 2 new programs per step, with steps at least 50 ms apart (about
0.5 s for the whole set), and keeps the same programs and keys. Desktop keeps the
single compile; `?precompile=all|N` overrides the budget. Peak three.js compiles
in any 100 ms went from 14-24 to at most 4, at start and after a restore. The
regression is pinned in `tests/e2e/touch-shader-warmup.spec.ts` (iphone project).

**Landmark factory street fix (2026-10-29, #105).** `factory.ts` `nearbyStreets` read the `streets-routing.json` paths as [lng, lat] when they are [lat, lng]. Every factory draft so far therefore had no named streets, and the likeness gate treated every non-blank wall group as street-facing. The #105 run installed nothing; its blockers are in TODO. Its crops are archived in source-data 4be52dd2a.

**Phones follow the street; the camera stops yawing at every wobble
(2026-10-29).** User: the mobile steering was "not fun to use and kind of
nauseating". Two causes in code: the chase camera eased toward the bike's
heading in ~0.25 s, so each thumb correction, road-guard nudge and on-the-spot
pivot yawed the whole city; and the analog stick turned straight into turn
rate, with diagonal gestures overloaded (brake, turn-around, pivot). Looked at
Mario Kart Tour (auto-cruise, one-finger sideways steer), Asphalt 9
TouchDrive (auto-steer, swipe to pick a route at forks) and SuperTuxKart
(wheel; tilt modes opt-in and fiddly). Built two things:
- `cameraYaw.ts`: heading-following views ignore changes under 10°, ease
  slower, and cap yaw at 80°/s (45°/s with reduced motion). The orbit bearing
  still applies at once on top, and the rotation is now wrapped to ±π.
- `streetFollow.ts`, control mode `street` ("Follow"), the default on
  phones/tablets (coarse pointer; keyboards keep Steer). The bike rides
  along the street by itself; ◀/▶ queue the next turn (one press, one turn;
  4 s memory), taken where a street opens on that side, with a slow-down on
  approach and the arc started at the radius the speed needs (committing at
  the corridor edge cut the corner at cruise). Straight on at crossings,
  bends followed, a T-junction or dead end waits; ↺ tap turns round, hold
  stops. Rides start parked until the first press, so the bike does not roll
  into the first question. A saved `relative` without the new version flag
  migrates once to `street` on touch.
`test:street-follow` rides real junctions without the road guard:
Leidsestraat × Keizersgracht (straight, left, right), the Keizersgracht ring
hands-off, Utrechtsestraat × Prinsengracht from past Kerkstraat; all stay in
the corridor, camera ≤ 80°/s, zero yaw on straight streets.

**Desktop draw spans and touch facade tiles (2026-10-29, #100 follow-up).** Ground and facade meshes now skip their off-screen parts. The whole-mesh draw call is unchanged; spans only cut the triangles drawn.

- **Desktop: spans.** The index buffer is reordered once, tile by tile, and each frame draws from the first to the last on-screen tile. Object and draw-call counts are unchanged, and the picture is pixel-identical at Westerkerk, Damrak, Dam and Leidseplein.
  - Ground: 1,065 → 609 k triangles at Westerkerk and 1,443 → 516 k at Leidseplein.
  - Facades: 1,493 → 724 k at Westerkerk and 1,571 → 461 k at Leidseplein.
  - An earlier version used separate tile meshes. It added about 65 draw calls and raised the three-layers time from 0.8 to 1.4 ms, so it was replaced by spans.
- **Touch: 3×3 tile meshes** that share the owner's buffers. iPad facades went from 596 → 245 k at Westerkerk, and the main pass is now 0.71–0.80 M triangles (1.13–1.36 M after #100).
  - Touch pictures can differ by 32–368 px at building seams, where draw order decides between coplanar neighbours.
- **Highlight passes** restore the full draw range after drawing.
- **Overrides:** `?groundTiles=1`, `?facadeTiles=1`, `?tileDraw=spans|tiles`.

**Manual catalogue deduplicated (2026-10-29).** Union merges had left four memorials in `manualCatalogue.json` several times over: johnny-jordaan-groep ×6, theo-thijssen-standbeeld ×5, carmiggelt-borstbeeld ×4 and winkler-prins-monument ×3. **Touch GPU load under target (2026-10-29, #100, CANAL-RECALL-7).** The iPad main pass at pitch 60 dropped from 1.7–1.9 M to 1.13–1.36 M triangles; the target was ≤ 1.5 M. Desktop is unchanged: same ground triangles, same meshes and the same 1,400 m ring.

- **Residency ring sized to the screen** (`residency.ts`, touch only). The farthest ground on screen is computed from the screen corners: 464 m on the iPad, which matches the measurement. The ring is that distance plus 25 m, rounded up to 100 m steps, plus 4 s of travel ahead (at most 400 m). That made the iPad ring 500 m instead of 800 m, with 3–4 cells loaded instead of 6–7. In a cap-speed ride at 117 m/s, missing ground at the screen edge fell from 65 samples to 4 out of 8,505. Override with `?groundRing=steps|view`.
- **Ground layers cut into culled tiles** (`cellTiles.ts`). A 1 km cell always counted as on screen. Layers over 4,000 triangles are now split into a 3×3 grid sharing the vertex buffers, and off-screen tiles are skipped. Ground at Westerkerk went from 875 k to 319 k triangles, for about 45 more draw calls. Override with `?groundTiles=1..4`.
- **Desktop trial:** `?groundTiles=3` cuts desktop ground by 56–74 % (Westerkerk 1,065 → 466 k, Leidseplein 1,443 → 371 k) with the same picture. Lever 1, road-polygon simplification, is deferred because the target was met without it.
- **Also fixed:** a De Pijp OSM leak. Three OSM ways (w277216400, w277216459, w277216482) inside the Ferdinand Bolstraat 12–22 row were still drawn through it. They are now suppressed.

**Westerpark West remainder: kit additions, nothing installed (2026-10-29, #97).**

- **`footprint: "core"`** (`coreFootprint.ts`). BAG traces an outline from above, so balcony-depth bumps on every storey (1.85 m on Blend) became full-height grooves. The core footprint snaps those bumps back onto the main wall and builds a clean box under the LoD2.2 roof. The pand's own OSM way is dropped as a false party wall.
- **`stackedBlocks` wall field** (`stackedBlocks.ts`). Rows of cells per storey: B is a block 1.5 m proud with 4-pane windows, R is a recessed balcony with a glass rail, `.` is plain wall. The footprint gates include the block outlines.
- **White-wall likeness rule** (`measureFacade.ts`, `wallIsOwnTrim`). A light, near-neutral wall that is its own bright reference is no longer exposure-darkened to grey. It is mapped to the 215 white point and never read lighter than raw. Across 1,532 archived large-recipe crops it fires on 97 and changes 33 by 3/255 or more, at most +33/255, all of them white or very light walls.
- **Blend (Haarlemmerweg 518, pand 0363100012250970)** is modelled and held. Its south, east and west faces were read from 2024-11-21 panoramas; the north face is inferred. Likeness has no evidence on any face:
  - `isLeaf` flags 49 % of the sunlit cream south wall as foliage;
  - the east and west crops are 48–50° oblique.

  The crops are archived in source-data dd929bb11.

- **GLB audit fix:** opening-outside now judges each coplanar wall piece where it meets the part. A front about 1° off its row was split into a 1.2 m piece and a 0.23 m strip, and judged 1.5 m away, which made a flush frieze read 3 cm proud. The 3 cm tolerance is unchanged, and a 6 cm part still fails.

**Centre feedback: one label per place, Beurs and Bijenkorf windows on their walls (2026-10-29, #94).**

- **d85ba0ac / 3702bcd7, double labels.** In Free Ride the DOM overlay repeated each canvas marker pill's name. `labels/labelDedupe.ts` `screenDuplicateIds` drops an overlay label that repeats a placed marker: the same landmark id, a similar name within 60 m, or a spelling variant within 600 m. `freeRide.ts` `secondMarkerIds` removes the inner-footprint second markers: Cuypersgebouw, Zuiderkerk Tower and OBA De Hallen.
- **58f97b44, Beurs.** Arches and clock plates hung 0.11–0.18 m off the walls. Tower arches were drawn on segments that run onto the 14 m roof. Each window now reads its local wall top. The GLB audit went from FAIL (11 hovering parts) to PASS.
- **3026cca1, Bijenkorf.** The Dam and Beursplein fronts stood 0.25–0.39 m behind the surveyed ring, so the brick swallowed the glass. The fronts are now fitted to the ring. Z-fighting went from 119 to 1.6 m².
- **59b67ef0, grey strip.** It was the generic `stair-glass` facade extra (p = 0.3), invented on Dam 2 and the 1991 corner beside the Bijenkorf. The panoramas show neither has one. The integrator removed the generic component; a real stair window comes from a building type.
- **Replay harness:** `tests/e2e/centre-feedback.spec.ts` replays each note's pose in Free Ride.

**Ferries dock at any pier; Odebrug reachable (2026-10-28, #93).** Feedback
50ea10bf, 1d632c41, f80d47da and 3e7f0aa4.

- **Docking radii,** measured from the OSM pier outlines:
  - On water a boat docks within 20 m of the stop. The Buiksloterweg pontoon, way 294911777, spans 11–23 m from it; the old radius was 6 m.
  - Touching land it docks within 37 m. The NDSM pier outline, way 588710849, reaches 36.8 m; the old radius was 16–20 m.
- **Any pier:** a boat docks at any ferry pier, not only its line's terminus. Players kept trying to step off at Buiksloterweg from an NDSM boat.
- **Re-arm hysteresis:** a pier within 50 m of the boarding point only becomes dockable once the boat has been 50 m away. So leaving Centraal F4 never docks at F3, 40 m along the same quay.
- **Hull on water:** the centre and both bow corners must stay on water. One bow corner on the bank turns the boat 4° away and slows it instead of stopping it.
- **Odebrug:** the cycle bridge Brug 228, way 1168346867, landed on a 1 m stub joined only to the sidewalks the extract drops. `routing/pavedLinks.ts` adds a curated rideable ring for that stub, indexed with the squares. Other cycleways that end on dropped footways need their own entries, or a generator that keeps connecting footways.
- **Regressions:** all pinned in `check-canal-car.ts`, the reachability audit and `ferry-docking-feedback.spec.ts`.
- **Still open:** only the bow is tested, so a hard turn can still swing a side over the quay.

**Own ground compiles half the shaders (2026-10-26).** Asking why phones that
lost their WebGL context (CANAL-RECALL-7) reported 66 three.js programs: a
phone-sized ride measured 68, all compiled within 10 s and none after. About 44
were the own-ground water-cut material, keyed by ground layer (asphalt, klinker,
lawn…) although its code depends only on the mask channel and the base
material's blend edit, plus each one's fade clone. Keying by
`base.customProgramCacheKey()` gives 32 programs on the same ride; each surface
keeps its own uniforms. Not shown to cause the context losses (the GPU name in
those reports is null because it is read after the loss), but it cuts start-up
compile work on every device.

**Shared frame survives a context lost mid-compile (2026-10-26).** Sentry
CANAL-RECALL-5 (Safari, Mac) regressed even though `renderPass` checks
`isContextLost()` before drawing: the context died between that check and
three's shader compile, so `createShader` answered null and `shaderSource`
threw from the animation frame. `renderLosingContext` now drops that frame
quietly when the flag has flipped or the error names a shader call; any other
error still throws. CANAL-RECALL-7/-J (context lost, then restored 1.4 s
later on Android 10 "K" phones, iPhones and Macs) are the expected diagnostics
and they show the restore working.

**Open squares are rideable (2026-10-26).** Feedback 636a57f4 (Dam) and
638590e9 (Leidseplein). `osm-loader.js` drops closed rings, so squares were
corridor-only. `src/canalRecall/routing/pedestrianAreas.ts` treats points
inside `squares.json` rings, at least 1.5 m from the edge, as on-road in
`getGuardRoad`. Excluded: rings under 250 m², names ending in plantsoen,
kerkhof, monument or hof, and lawn squares (Frederiksplein, Museumplein,
Cantaplein). Routing-extract pedestrian rings stay unused because the
`area` tag is dropped, so a ring could be a block loop. Regressions are in
check-canal-car (Dam ride, Leidseplein exits, Frederiksplein and the Piet
Heinkade loop blocked) plus e2e `open-squares.spec.ts`. Also: Sentry
CANAL-RECALL-H guarded (`inspectBuilding` after a WebGL context loss).

**White flash on governor steps (2026-10-25, #64).** User saw random white
flashes. The render governor called `setPixelRatio` inside MapLibre's
`render` event, after the frame was drawn; the resize cleared the buffer and
the paper body background (#f4efe5) showed for one frame (screencast luma
0.89 vs 0.48, 17–37 ms after each step; a fast Mac rarely steps, hence
"random"). Steps now apply at the next frame start with `setPixelRatio` +
`redraw`. Regression `tests/e2e/governor-no-flash.spec.ts` (old bundle 0.927
worst, fixed 0.50); opt-in probe `white-flash-probe.spec.ts`. Desktop perf
unchanged. Context loss still shows paper for its whole duration (no Sentry
events); a mid-tone `#vector-map` background is the cheap mitigation.

## Landmarks stop piling up, and nothing loads behind the setup card (2026-10-23)

Users reported the game crashing phones and running far too slowly on ordinary
computers. Sentry had the evidence: a Safari/Mac session (CANAL-RECALL-5, -4)
lost its WebGL context after 30 landmark GLBs landed in 30 s, spread across the
whole centre (Begijnhof, Madame Tussauds, Fatih Moskee, the Dam). The landmark
layer loaded every model that came into view and never gave one back; only a
street-chunk swap ever dropped an entry, so residency grew with the ride.

- **Eviction** (`landmarks/landmarkResidency.ts`): above a resident budget (24 on
  touch, 72 on desktop; `?landmarkBudget=`) the furthest off-view models give
  their extrusion back, down to budget − 4, at most twice a second. In-view,
  highlighted, mid-level-swap and procedural building-type entries never go.
  An evicted model reloads (HTTP cache) when it is in view again.
  `_signatureLandmarks.evictions` counts them.
- **No loading below z15**: the overview raster draws the city to z15.6, and
  below z15 "visible" meant every landmark in Amsterdam.
- **Nothing behind the setup card**: the default Damrak view pulled in 21
  landmark GLBs behind the route card, which covers the whole screen on a
  phone. The layer is now built suspended; `sync` resumes it when the start
  flight lands, as it already did after the flight.

Measured with `tests/e2e/phone-memory.spec.ts` (iPhone profile, forced GC per
sample): setup 21 → 0 landmarks; a ride's first 10 s draws 30 and gives back
15–18. After GC the live heap is flat at ~330 MB over a 30 s ride — the 4 MB/s
growth seen without GC is per-frame garbage, not a leak. GPU at the Dam:
~60 MB textures, ~130–150 MB buffers; landmarks hold 16 MB of that, the own
ground ~57 MB of buffers and ~28 MB of textures (`?ownGround=0`). Live heap at
ride start is dominated by whole-city roads (road-network segment geometry
47 MB, road graph 43 MB, OSM loader 23 MB) and the own ground (28 MB).

A 1 km own-ground cap on phones saved only 18 MB (9 cells instead of 11;
~12 MB of geometry per cell) and the far ring is off at chase zoom, so phones
keep the default ring; `?groundRadius=N` fixes the ring for A/B shots.

## Slow machines step their render cost down (2026-10-23)

"Fine on my M4": desktop renders at the full device pixel ratio with MSAA and a
2048² shadow map, so a laptop at 150–200 % scaling with an integrated GPU draws
2.25–4× the pixels of a 1× canvas. `renderGovernor.ts` watches the map's render
cadence while riding (game state 4 only; loading and the intro fly-in do not
count) and after two consecutive slow windows (90 frames or 1.5 s, whichever
comes first; p75 over 26 ms; intervals over 1 s are a hidden tab) steps:
pixel ratio ×0.75 down to 1, then sun shadows off, then 0.75× only if p75 is
over 40 ms. It never steps back up; a pause or leaving the ride resets the run.
`?governor=0` turns it off, an explicit `?dpr=` keeps its ratio. Steps log
`[canal-recall] render budget step`; status is `vectorMap._renderGovernor`.
Shipped in `map-guard.bundle.js` (entry `mapHealthBrowser.ts`). On the M4 it
never steps. `tests/e2e/weak-gpu-perf.spec.ts` (SwiftShader, 1440×900 at
1.5×) is the weak-GPU proxy: it runs at ~2 fps, so it ranks costs rather than
predicting a laptop. Median frame 507 ms default, 332 ms at `?dpr=1` (−35 %),
286 ms with `?msaa=0`; shadows-off was bimodal and inconclusive. It also caught
the first governor draft never stepping there (90-frame windows and a 250 ms gap
cutoff); with time-bounded windows it went 1.5 → 1.13 → 1 inside a 12 s ride.
iOS Low Power Mode caps rAF at 30 fps, so the governor also steps there.

## Phones render fewer pixels, and a lost GPU now says why (2026-10-23)

Follow-up to the dead-GPU guard. Measured on the production ride with a Pixel 5
profile (Chromium, counting resident GL objects, not upload traffic): the setup
screen holds 11 MB of textures and 10 MB of buffers, a started ride settles at
47 MB of textures and 90 MB of buffers with a 150–210 MB JS heap, and it
plateaus at about 20 s — the moment the "crashes after ~20 s" reports describe.
MapLibre's logged failure was earlier (a dead GPU process at ~5 s, before the
heavy content), so these are two different events: the first is a driver /
GPU-process failure that can only be tolerated, the second is memory pressure.

Three phone budgets, each with an override for A/B shots:
- `pixelRatio` on coarse pointers goes 1.5 → 1.25 (`?dpr=`). On a 390×844 phone
  that is −31% pixels in the drawing buffer, its MSAA and the fill rate.
- MSAA is off when `navigator.deviceMemory` reports ≤3 GB (`?msaa=0/1`):
  Android's low-memory killer is where phone GPU processes usually go.
- Resident z14 building tiles go 12 → 9 on touch (`?tileBudget=`; exposed as
  `status().budget`). The 3D city chunks are per tile, so this is the main
  geometry lever behind the 90 MB of in-ride buffers.

And the missing evidence: `mapGuard` now reports `webglcontextlost` as its own
one-shot Sentry warning even when no shader threw, carrying the GPU renderer and
vendor, `performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize`, `navigator.deviceMemory`,
`hardwareConcurrency`, the canvas CSS/backing sizes and the drawing buffer. The
next phone crash will say whether it was the GPU process or memory, and on
which hardware. Before this the only options were a shader throw or silence.

Verified: `npm run test:map-guard` (7 tests), `tsc`, and Playwright on the local
ride — backing ratio 1.249 by default (`?dpr=1.5` still 1.499), one context-loss
report with the full payload after two events, `status().budget` 9 — and the
explorer still wraps its map. The DPR/MSAA changes still need a real
iPhone/Android pass before they can be called done.

## The land stops poking through the grass (2026-10-23)

Follow-up to the Rembrandtplein cut: beige specks inside the lawns were the bare
land grid showing through the green. A fill drapes the 5 m land grid at its own
vertices, so where the grid crests, the plane between them dips under it — 7 cm
at p99, 15 cm at p99.9, 73 cm at the worst bank — and the land won the depth
test. `drapeBisect` now splits a fill triangle whose plane would sit more than
2 mm under the land at a land grid node inside it (over one grid cell both are
planes, so the deepest sag is at a node, or where a triangle edge crosses a grid
line), down to 1 m edges; the far ring allows 1 cm. Green nodes in the
Vondelpark cell with land above the fill: 355 over 2 cm and 144 over 5 cm
before, 6 and 1 after; p99 7.0 cm → 0.1 cm. Triangles cost 1–10 % (crests pay).
Regression test on the streamed Vondelpark cell; the ground-places shots gained
the Blauwe Theehuis.

## A dead GPU no longer floods the ride with shader errors (2026-10-23)

Sentry CANAL-RECALL-1 (`Error: Could not compile fragment shader: `, 7 events,
1–2 devices over six days) was not a shader bug. The empty info log is the
signature of a dead GPU process: every GL query answers 0/false and
`isContextLost()` only flips a moment later. MapLibre 5.24.0 reads
`COMPILE_STATUS` straight after `compileShader` and throws from
`Painter.useProgram` inside the animation frame; because a failed program is
never cached, it rebuilds and throws the same error every frame. The Android
event logged 94 of them in 20 s, on both the ride raster layer and (on a
different release) the `explore` map. Both affected devices were low-end/older
Android (Firefox Mobile 158 on Android 17; Chrome Mobile 155 on Android 10),
which is consistent with the GPU process dying under memory pressure rather
than with anything in our style.

Upstream #8607 describes the same failure and was fixed in maplibre-gl 6.13.0
(#8633): link first, and treat a failed link with zero attached shaders as a
context loss instead of throwing. We still pin 5.24.0 (the last 5.x, April
2026), and 6.x is ESM-only with `map.transform` removed, so a bump is a
migration rather than a version change. `src/canalRecall/mapGuard.ts` therefore
applies the 6.13 rule around `map._render` now: only empty-log compile/link
errors are swallowed, drawing pauses for 2 s so `webglcontextlost` can arrive,
the loop retries once, one Sentry message carries `RENDERER`/`VENDOR`/
`isContextLost`, and a reload notice appears if the GPU never returns. Errors
with a real GLSL log still throw. The ride (`vector-map.js`) and the explorer
(`explorer/browser.ts`) install it; `monitoring.ts` also drops empty-log shader
errors from Sentry as a backstop for unguarded demo pages.

Verified: `npm run test:map-guard` (dead-GPU signature, real-log errors,
single report, frame hold and retry) and Playwright against the local ride and
explore pages — both maps wrap `_render`, a simulated `webglcontextlost` shows
the notice after 8 s, `webglcontextrestored` clears it, and neither page logs a
page error. The tab crash itself is the GPU process dying; this stops the
error storm and lets MapLibre's own loss/restore path run, but it does not make
a broken GPU render. Migrate to ≥6.13 or finish the drop-MapLibre lane (TODO).

## The ride's errors finally point at TypeScript (2026-10-23)

Map Quest had Sentry source maps since the monitoring work; the ride did not.
Its scripts are esbuild IIFE bundles in `public/canal-drive/js/`, built with
`--minify` and no `--sourcemap`, and the deploy uploaded only `dist-quiz`. Every
error from rideamsterdam.nl/ride arrived as minified frames with no artifact in
the `canal-recall` project, while `src/canalRecall/monitoring.ts` still tagged
the release with the commit SHA — so releases looked connected and nothing
symbolicated. Now every bundle that writes into `public/canal-drive/js/` builds
with external maps (no `sourceMappingURL` comment, so nothing points at them),
`scripts/sentry/collect-canal-bundles.mjs` stages the scripts `index.html`
actually loads plus their maps, and the deploy injects debug IDs, uploads them
to `canal-recall`, copies the injected scripts back over `dist/`, and deletes
every `.map` before the site is assembled. The collector fails when a ride
bundle has no map, so a new build step cannot quietly regress to minified
frames. Only ride scripts are uploaded: the galleries never initialise
monitoring, so their maps would be sent on every deploy for nothing. The four
ride bundles that used to be built out of band — collection, tours, street
overlay style, signature placement — are now part of `npm run build` too, so a
deploy cannot ship an older copy of one of them without a map. (They rebuilt
byte-identical to the committed files on 2026-10-23, so nothing served changed.)

## The square stops flickering green through its grass (2026-10-23)

User: "what are these green patches and why are they wiggling?" — the mapped
grass beds on Rembrandtplein, drawn flat by the own ground. The OSM square's
paved area and the grass area inside it are two fills of the same relief, each
draped on its own triangulation, so on a few metres of slope their heights
cross (measured ±13 mm at Rembrandtplein); the square sits 4 mm higher with the
same draw rank, and at 300 m one depth quantum is ~4 mm, so the pair
interleaved per triangle and the grass shimmered through the paving in shards
that crawled with the camera (worst at the low chase pitch). Every paved area
fill now cuts the OSM green rings out of its triangulation (`groundCell.ts`
`greenCuts`/`holesIn`, earcut holes): nothing is drawn over the grass, so
there is no coplanar pair to fight over, and the grass reads as its mapped
shape. A ring the BGT survey re-draws (parks-v1, which culls the OSM green fill
under it) keeps its paving, or the cut would expose the land. New
`stats.greenCut`; regression test on the streamed Rembrandtplein cell; shots in
`artifacts/ground-places/{before,after}/rembrandtplein.png`
(`node scripts/ground-places-shots.mjs <tag> "?ownGround=1&sharedFrame=1" rembrandtplein`).

## 2026-10-21 — rideamsterdam.nl moves to Cloudflare Pages

Firebase was on the free plan (360 MB/day of Hosting transfer), and one ride
downloads ~14 MB (landing 0.5 MB, setup 7.8 MB, start + 25 s of riding
14.3 MB, measured with CDP on the live site), so a Reddit post would have
shut the site off within minutes. The user chose Cloudflare Pages over
Firebase Blaze, Vercel (same per-GB price plus a fee) and S3/CloudFront.
`scripts/hosting/build-pages-site.mjs` derives the Pages build and its
`_redirects`/`_headers` from firebase.json; two Pages behaviours needed
handling (rules run before static files, so `/quiz/*` swallowed Map Quest's
JS until pass-through rules were generated; no `404.html` means every
missing file is a 200 landing page). `canal-site.spec.ts` passed 8/8 in
`wrangler pages dev` and again against production `rideamsterdam.pages.dev`.
Uploading from the Mac stalled (14 of 7,234 files in minutes, connection
resets, no rate limiting): CI deploys instead. Gotchas: the `cf` CLI's OAuth
login cannot mint API tokens (the user made one in the dashboard);
`wrangler pages project create` ran Cloudflare's auto-setup, which rewrote
package.json, the lockfile and vite.config.ts and replaced the node_modules
symlink with a real install (all reverted; use `cf pages projects create`).
Nameservers switched at Porkbun via its API to the Cloudflare zone; Firebase
still receives every deploy as a fallback.

## Postcards need spaced recall (2026-10-17)

The user found postcards too easy ("16 of 78" after little play). Before, any
neighbourhood review state with repetitions ≥ 1 earned one, so a single good
Pinpoint (≤ ~535 m) or a correct 4-choice Guess Name did; the ride never wrote
neighbourhood states (the bike mark is drawn on every card, earned or not).
Now `postcardProgress` in `src/mapRecall/progress.ts` requires recalls on two
different days with at least one pin ≤ 250 m, or a precise pin (≤ 60 m) plus a
correct answer ≥ 30 min later, or Guess Name on three different days; synced
states without a local event log need three good answers in a row. Earned
cards are never revoked by a later miss. In-progress buurten show faded with
"1 of 2 days"; the end screen announces only cards the session completed.
Existing players lose cards that no longer qualify (derived state).

## Statue rebuild comparison: TRELLIS.2 multi-view beats the kit on 17 of 20 (2026-10-17)

User (2026-10-17), after "these are a little rough": "honestly can we rebuild
those statues? did we ever try trellis? is tripo still better?". Lane
`lane/statue-rebuild-20261017` (133e452f5, 7f57ed792, c51f57d60). TRELLIS.2
multidiffusion (MLX port) on 3–5 licensed Commons photos beats both the figure
kit and single-view TripoSR wherever 3 or more side views exist; TripoSR stays
for single-view stone groups (the Kinderbrug) and the Sarphati bust. Verdicts
at gallery size: 17 better (Lieverdje, Anne Frank Merwedeplein, Multatuli,
Wilhelmina, Vondel, Dokwerker, Thorbecke slightly, Teun de Jager, Johnny
Jordaan group in five runs, Theo Thijssen as one casting, Carmiggelt, Gandhi,
Rembrandt statue, Sarphati bust, Spanjemonument, both Kinderbrug groups); no
better: Spinoza (head becomes a hood), Mama Baranka (rough-cast bronze gives
see-through holes); worse: Waterdraagster (TripoSR tilts it). Pipeline
`scripts/sculptures/rebuild.ts`: Commons fetch with licence gate and author
(429 retry-after, 1.2–1.5 s spacing), cut-outs (isnet or u2net per view),
reconstruction under a one-TRELLIS lock (18 GB free), decimation to ~6k tris
into the kit's material slot (no photo colour), kit surgery keeping plinths
and architecture (`kitParts.ts`), and a photo | kit | rebuild sheet
(`docs/images/sculptures/<id>-rebuild.jpg`). Provenance with sculptor, death
year and PD status per statue in `scripts/sculptures/rebuild-sources/`. TRELLIS
puts the first photo on −y; silhouette orientation cannot tell front from back
on dark bronze (Wilhelmina and Spanjemonument set by eye). Nothing installed:
the GLBs are in the lane's artifacts/ for the user's pick. Only Vondel,
Thorbecke, Rembrandt and Sarphati are by sculptors dead over 70 years.

## Tropenmuseum brick: measured in diffuse light, rose-brown not tan (2026-10-17)

User (2026-10-16/17): the Tropenmuseum read tan-brown against the card photo's
rosier brick; "figure it out". Lane `worktree-agent-a71864c1df179c607`: the
colour, not the lighting. The brick carries little colour of its own (chroma
~10), so its hue follows the light: every panorama crop and sunlit photo reads
Lab hue 55-65, diffuse photos from four photographers (card photo included)
hue 2-35. The old #a2856c was a sun reading, and the rig's warm sun added the
warmth again; the tint method keeps hue (uniform linear gain) and the crops were
not contaminated (brick-only re-measure ~58). In-game frames match plain diffuse
shading under SUNNY_LIGHT (shade x0.563, chroma -28 %, hue within 3 degrees) on
the controls too (Oosterparkkerk, Hoofdbureau: photos and panoramas agree), so
it is a Tropenmuseum colour, not a citywide bias. New `look/brickTone.ts`
(brick-only crop measure, sun/diffuse classification from the pale trim,
`brickAlbedo`: diffuse crops, one vote per camera, calibrated lightness; 8
tests) and `scripts/look/measure-brick-tone.ts`, `brick-tone-frames.ts`. Brick
#a28382 (hue 23, chroma 12.7); GLB geometry unchanged. Trade-off: sunlit walls
read pinker (hue 38) than real sunlit photos (55-63), the rig's sun being less
warm than real sun against skylight; left alone (the "One wall material" pass).
Sheets: `artifacts/brick-tone/` in the lane worktree.

Canal CI had failed on every push since 2026-10-16 evening, so the GitHub Pages
deploy (gated on a green CI) was skipped each time while Firebase kept deploying.

`artifacts/haparandaweg/spots.json` at module load, before its `test.skip`, so the
full e2e job crashed at collection (ENOENT); it now reads the file only with
`HAP_SHOTS`. And holding the Kinderbrug statue model (2026-10-17) took its POI
out of the game, orphaning its card override (`osm_artwork_4370460330`);
`test:landmark-cards` now accepts an override whose kit model is held.
The next run showed two more: `street-chunks.spec.ts` read `chunk.instance` at
load though chunks.json no longer holds a `chunk-bilder-*` chunk (now skipped
when absent; `playwright test --list` collects all 986 tests), and eight new
Boterdiep/Hoendiep block faces had no `chunkWallExposureData.ts` entry
(regenerated from their strips; the 42 existing entries unchanged). Installs
must re-run `scripts/look/build-chunk-wall-exposure.ts --write`.
Even green, Pages would not deploy: three sessions pushed more often than a CI
run takes (~8 min) and `cancel-in-progress` cancelled every main run before it
finished. CI now lets a main run finish (GitHub keeps one pending, the newest);
pull requests still cancel.
The first run allowed to finish then failed `check:landmark-inventory`: 309 of
434 landmarks "first exported 2026-10-17". The gate dates a model by the commit
that first added its GLB, and CI's shallow checkout had one commit. The
check:canal job now checks out the history without blobs (`fetch-depth: 0`,
`filter: blob:none`), and the gate refuses a shallow clone instead of misdating.
With check:canal green on CI, the full Playwright job still blocked Pages: on a
hosted runner it reached 13 of 121 spec files in its 40 min and timed out, with
failures in askable-bridges, answered-street-name, block-face and others. It
moved to its own workflow, `e2e-full.yml` (nightly 03:00 UTC and on demand,
180 min); Canal CI is check:canal plus the boot smoke, the same bar as the
Firebase deploy.
Block-face installs kept skipping the exposure step (Gorontalo, Molukken, Nias,
Hembrug, Polanen, Houtrijk, Zaanhof: 18 faces on 2026-10-17), each time turning
CI red; `block-face/compile.ts --install` now runs
`build-chunk-wall-exposure.ts --write` itself.

municipal register) were taught by no question. `askableBridges.ts`: every
bridge-named routed way joins `bridges.json` except register numbers, decks
shorter than the 8 m route-question settle distance, and a second OSM spelling
within 150 m. 300 → 416 bridges, 0 existing ids lost (the generator's own hash
reproduces all 300; only `distractors` changed, on 128), 116 new crossings all
over mapped water (85 named), 98 new register descriptions; 363 reach the quiz
at load. Excluded: nine short decks (Spiegelbrug 6.5 m … Kanaalpost 4.3 m) and
Heiligewegssluis (variant of Heiligewegsluis, 6 m apart). New bridges are not
notable, so they are asked at hard/expert/custom only. `build-askable-bridges.ts`
stages and `--publish`es the four extract files together; the generator applies
the same rule on refresh. Culverts without a suffix (Bullebak, Kanaalpost,
Postje van Gerrit Vreling) are decks via `UNSUFFIXED_DECK_NAMES`. The street
plaque reads the carried street (`routePlaqueName`, same withholding rule as
any street), so it is no longer blank on a carrying deck. Riding the
Noordsche Compagniebrug and Niek Engelschmanbrug now also asks the canal
crossed; `turn-question-timing.spec.ts` accepts that ask. Regressions:
`test:bridge-street-name` (13), `check-canal-car.ts` named cases,
`askable-bridges.spec.ts`. Lane `fix/bridge-names-quiz-20261016`.

## Pop-in: streaming look-ahead, a basemap hold, chunk dissolve; a houseboat freeze fixed (2026-10-16)

User (2026-10-16): "there's a lot of pop-in in the game, is that something
we can improve without harming perf?". Lane `lane/pop-in-20261016`
(2c15ac288 metric, bef643cdb, f7484e12f, 35e77cf11, b2e717abd, afe9f2636,
02acc7256, 63f23d0a5); doc `docs/perf-pop-in-20261016.md`. A pop-in metric
(camera-compensated per-frame residual blobs on a scripted ride, attributed
to their source) found a freeze first: a houseboat chunk's highlight pass
read vertex arrays three.js had freed (`TypeError` every frame on the boat
route; regression test). Fixes, each with an off switch: look-ahead steered
by the rider's heading (`streamingLookAhead.ts`: building tiles 5–12 s
ahead, facade chunks nearest-ahead first, the own-ground worker queue drops
left cells and builds ahead-first; `?lookAhead=0`); the basemap's buildings
hold until a coarse shell under the rider is installed, 400 ms after the
first shell, or 8 s (`__canalRecallHoldBasemap=false`); a first version
waited on off-screen shells and showed the city ~1 s late at light load,
caught at integration and fixed); arriving facade chunks dissolve in over
350 ms (`?chunkFade=0`). Loaded machine, start of ride: building pop-in
14,429 → 593 px/s, ground-cell latency 8.6 → 3.3 s. Light load: first real
city 0.3 s either way, attributed pop-in 250 → 124 px/s (CPU ×2: 912 →
182). Desktop motion: longest frame 33 ms, p95 16.8 ms; facade geometry
140 → 200 MB resident. Gate: `tests/e2e/pop-in.spec.ts` (`PERF_POPIN=1`,
≤ 1000 px/s, ground-cell latency median ≤ 1500 ms).

`parapet()` drew each side over the whole measured deck span, which runs metres
past the water onto the quays, where `deckWidths` pulls the edge in to the road
half-width: the railing turned 90° across footway and cycle lane and ran along
the carriageway (BRU0166 Nassaukade/Bilderdijkgracht; BRU0063 down into the
road). Lane `worktree-agent-ace959b5342296a67`: `railingRuns.ts` keeps each
side where its edge meets the water (+1.5 m onto the abutment), breaks at gates
(>45° over >0.75 m), folds and long dry stretches, and never stands on a bridge
way crossing the parapet line. Citywide (`check:bridge-railings`): bridges with
a gate 559 → 12, lateral gate run 6,473 → 76 m, parapet inside a carriageway or
cycle polygon 50 bridges / 568 m → 6 / 75 m (roads-v1 pilot cells). Regressions
BRU0166, BRU0063, BRU0257 in `check:own-ground-cells`, unit tests, e2e
`BRIDGES=RAILINGS`; checked against PDOK orthophoto crops.

## Neck and bell gables curve the right way: concave shoulders, measured from the photo (2026-10-16)

User (2026-10-16), on a Wallen review sheet: "weird that the kit inverts the
curve of the roof from concave to convex or vice versa". Lane
`lane/gable-curves-20261016` (1599228cb). Cause in `fit.ts crownProfile`:
neck flanks used `shoulderCurve 0.6` (f^0.6) and bell flanks fell back to
`sin(f·π/2)`, both bulging outward; real claw pieces and bell flares stay
low at the foot and rise steeply into the neck (Oudezijds Achterburgwal
177920: the claw 0.05–0.4 m over the eaves until 0.2 m from the neck).
New `crownShoulder: 'concave' | 'ogee' | 'straight' | 'convex'` on the
front intent (neck/bell), default concave (quarter ellipse tangent to the
neck); landmark builders without the option stay byte-identical.
`gableFromStrip.flankCurvature` measures each flank against its chord: 19
of 25 measured bell/neck fronts read concave (Utrechtsestraat 66-68 set
`straight`). Roofs over the crowns: `roof-under-crown` sampled only 5 mm
inside the facade, so an attic standing 1.5–2.8 m over the shoulders
passed; `roofAboveCrownFrontView` now checks the whole plot square to the
frontage and a new `roof-behind-crown` gate checks the chunk; saddles
behind full-front neck/bell crowns may drop to 3 m below the cornice at the
party walls; every own roof sits under its crown. Reinstalled
wallen-oza-41-57, wallen-ozv-115-125, utrechtse-48-76, nassau-162289,
bilder-164451-156126, bilder-233580-162444. Still open: a neighbour's roof
behind an oblique party wall showing beside a crown (177915 by 177916,
2.9 m), step/spout/point gables not yet under the front-view check
(bilder-081118-155417), and the kit cannot yet say neck width (fixed 0.5 of
the front; photos 0.38–0.45), claw height, a cornice band and pediment
wider than the neck, an inset foot ledge, or a mansard with hipped sides.

over 1,243 m²; named regression in `towerPodium.test.ts` (now in

## A bridge deck is never the answer to "which street?" (2026-10-16)

User (2026-10-16), riding the Raadhuisstraat over the Keizersgracht: "the game
asks me what street am I on when I'm on this bridge, and the correct answer is a
brug". `_updateCanalQuiz` (`recallRuntime.ts`) settled the route question on the
way's own OSM name, and OSM names that deck "Niek Engelschmanbrug". The
deliberate bridge question only knows the 300 curated `bridges.json` bridges, so
123 other bridge names were asked as streets (the 2026-10-09 spec even pinned
"asks the Noordsche Compagniebrug as a street"). `bridgeStreetName.ts`: a way named
…brug/…sluis/…duiker/Brug N (not Brugstraat, Oudebrugsteeg) answers with the one
street that continues in line (45°) at both ends, following decks split mid-span
and ignoring quays that meet at ~90° (Grote Brouwerssluis → Prinsengracht,
Vingboomsbrug → Huidenstraat). With no single carried street the deck is
transparent and the street beyond is asked ~8 m after it (Westermarkt → Niek
Engelschmanbrug → Raadhuisstraat). Askable `bridges.json` bridges keep "Which
bridge are you on?". Citywide: 436 bridge-named ways under 194 names, 126 ways
now carry a street and 310 are transparent; the Raadhuisstraat, Leidsestraat and
Utrechtsestraat radial decks are already mapped under the street's name.
Regressions: `check-canal-car.ts` (both reported bridges, the two carried
cases, no bridge-named way ever a street answer citywide),
`turn-question-timing.spec.ts` rides both decks, `test:bridge-street-name`
(in `check:canal`).

## Landmark cards: sourced English facts, and an audit for bare definitions and leftover Dutch (2026-10-16)

User (2026-10-16), on the Huis Bartolotti arrival card: "this is a really
uninspiring fact for this house that has a whole wikipedia page". The card
read "Het Huis Bartolotti (also Het Bonte Huis) is a canal house at
Herengracht 170-172". Three causes. `splitDetail` (`landmarkData.ts`) keeps
whole sentences up to 280 characters, so a long second sentence leaves the
bare first one. The arrival card reads the raw landmark (`presentationRuntime.ts`
`_finishLandmark`), not the rotated trivia notice, so the three published
Bartolotti facts never reach it. And `protectNames` (`scripts/lib/translation.ts`)
keeps the Dutch article in front of a protected name ("Het [Huis Bartolotti]").
Lane `lane/landmark-card-text-20261016`: `landmark-card-overrides.json` holds 43
curated English cards (Bartolotti first: built c. 1617 for Willem van den Heuvel,
who took the name Bartolotti to inherit, attributed to Hendrick de Keyser, bending
twice with the Herengracht), each with source URL, article, language, the
verbatim original passages (Dutch kept), licence and the text it replaces.
`audit:landmark-cards --publish` writes them into `funFact` and the drive-by
`opening`; the published diff is exactly 43 `funFact`/`funFactSourceUrl` and 43
`opening` fields, `wikipediaExtract` untouched. `landmarkCardAudit.ts` and
`test:landmark-cards` (now in `check:canal`) flag definitional-only and
Dutch-leaking cards; Bartolotti is the named regression. Over 537 cards: 139
flagged before (45 definitional, 3 Dutch, 92 empty), 96 after (4, 0, 92).
Re-run `--publish` after any extract regeneration or `facts:attach-openings
--force`.

## One model per ground: the Wereldmuseum drew twice (2026-10-16)

User (2026-10-16), with two ride screenshots of the Mauritskade portal:
"wereld frontage issues - why not caught?". Two models stood on the KIT
complex: `wereldmuseum-amsterdam` (2026-10-04 massing) and `tropenmuseum`
(the measured 2026-10-14 model), same landmark, 38 shared suppressed ids,
both in `GAME_BUILDING_MODELS`. Not caught because the Tropenmuseum lane
added a new id instead of holding the old one, every review rendered one
GLB alone (`landmark-strip`, `review:sheet`), and the suppression checks
only compare models against OSM/BAG, which both passed. The old entry is now
`status: "held"` with a `heldReason`. `modelOverlap.ts` and its test
(`test:building-taxonomy`, in `check:canal`) fail when two drawn models share
a landmark id or a suppressed OSM way / BAG pand. Across 485 drawn models it
found one more pair: Brandweerkazerne Nico (`fire-station-nico`, every side
modelled) and the 2026-10-13 Politiebureau IJ-tunnel large recipe on the same
1972 pand (three sides blank). The landmark wins: `SHADOWED_BY_LANDMARK` in
`ordinaryModels.ts` keeps the install catalogued but undrawn, and the test
fails if a pair goes stale. (`royal-palace` in `signature-landmarks.json` is
a stale manifest record, not drawn.) `review:sheet` now puts an IN GAME
tile on every wall row (one browser, a 70° frame of that wall), not one
overhead shot of the main wall; `docs/buildings-pipeline.md` (bespoke lane,
items 7-8) requires both. Correction to the first diagnosis: with the old
model gone, the in-game frames of the Mauritskade face still show what the
user saw. The plain brown walls with bare blue cells either side of the portal
are the Tropenmuseum's own kit walls, so that face goes to the fourth pass
(TODO).

## Buurt coverage in the app, and the first buurt generator pilot (Bellamybuurt-Zuid) (2026-10-16)

User (2026-10-16), on the coverage map: "would be nice if this was bundled
into our app … I'd love to be able to click on a neighborhood and explore
its kits". `coverage.html` (lane/coverage-app-20261016, 0fc950d7c data,
0b57e6fa4 page; linked from What's new, Street surveys and the chunks lab):
the buurt map coloured by modelled share or "what we have"; click, search
or `?buurt=<code>` opens a panel with the tier counts, top uncovered repeat
clusters, the type libraries whose evidence pands stand there (swatches,
kit keys, exemplar pands, source faces), block faces (installed ones link
to `street-chunks.html?only=…`), recipe and ordinary models, landmark
kits, building-type designs with an inline 3D preview, and the street
surveys. `buurten.json` carries per-buurt id lists (603 KB); names, links
and thumbnails sit in `contents.json` (254 KB) loaded on the first click;
the build verifies every link and thumbnail on disk. A buurt with nothing
says so and names its biggest uncovered cluster. 312 of 518 buurten have
something, but 210 only through generic landmark kits: 122 have more than
landmarks, 18 block-face work, 23 building-type designs, 206 nothing.
Gaps: no exemplar photo crops ship under `public/`, building-type designs
have no thumbnails, `street-surveys` data dates from 10-10.

Buurt generator pilot (lane/buurt-generator-20261016, f6dcd8527; doc
`docs/buurt-generator-20261016.md`), answering "how close are we to being
able to cheaply install generators in places like this?":
`block-face:buurt-survey` proposes 97 street-side faces from shared party
walls and intakes the uncovered ones (49, ~85 s each);
`block-face:auto-place` (`blockFace/autoPlace.ts`) scores every library
type per pand (hard vetoes year ±2, frontage ±0.4 m; storeys from eaves,
3DBAG storeys and roof form, measured wall colour and stucco, bands,
window columns, white-bay side and share), mirrors from door/bay side,
takes the crown from the photo skyline and a shopfront from BAG/OSM, then
gates on an edge likeness (`stripLikeness.ts`, floor 0.15) with every
rival type compiled on the same runs (held if a rival scores > 0.05
higher). New kit component `tilePanels` (`buildingRecipe/tileAccents.ts`:
yellow pier diamonds, green sill tiles) and six measured types in
`scripts/block-face/types/bellamy/`. Result: 102 of 335 pands placed on 17
faces, the rest held with reasons; 31 faces place nothing because their
designs are not in the library. Five rows get a wrong type that still
passes the gate (Jan Hanzenstraat 49–51, Ten Katestraat 29–31,
Bellamystraat 18–20, Hasebroekstraat 69, Van Effenstraat 7D), so nothing
is installed: the gate cannot yet certify a match. The kit still cannot
say Hasebroekstraat 56–70's white painted timber oriels or its white
cornice with hoist-cap dormers, a window kind per axis, double house
doors, or balconies read from the strip. Cost: the survey, intake and
placement are machine time (~150 s for a full placement run) a Haiku lane
can drive; authoring types (10–20 min each, measuring is what pays: the
flat row's score 0.05 → 0.55), kit components and gallery-size review
need an Opus lane.

## Map labels hide under the loading screen (2026-10-16)

User report, with a screenshot of "Finding your way..." over Boom Chicago,
Electric Ladyland and the Kazerne Hendrik labels: "don't show destinations
through scrim". The DOM label overlay (`src/canalRecall/labels/labelOverlay.ts`)
sits above the game canvas so it can share the HUD's collision rules, which
also put it above the opaque paper the canvas paints for the menu, route setup
and loading screen; it kept placing the start area's venues there.
`isCoveredState` (MENU, MAP_SELECT, LOADING) now hides the overlay root. The
check runs in the map's render frame and on its own 150 ms clock, since a state
change need not repaint the map. `tests/e2e/labels.spec.ts` "hidden while the
loading screen covers the map" watches every frame of a route load: the old
bundle showed labels in 289 loading frames, the fix shows none.

## Roofs follow the front: the step-gable library bug, saddles under crowns, row coherence; 232 of 371 pands change class (2026-10-16)

Lane `lane/kit-roof-rules-20261016` (1dd7652e9 planner export and
`roof-golden`, 83ea726a9 schema, 777cfb967/bdd6f374b merge and golden
re-record, 53546a733 front forms, bd2483736 the library fix, 2fff8e30f
the rules; doc `docs/front-roofs-20261016.md`), from the user's three
corrections. **The lopsided step gables were a library bug**:
`canalhouseCrownProfile('trap')`'s right-flank loop ran one tread late,
so every step gable in the library leaned by one tread (0.38 m on
Kinkerstraat 68); `fit-golden.json` re-recorded for exactly the five
step-gable houses (bilder-155418/156286/156287, cw-heren-175702/179665),
151 identical; `gableSymmetry.test.ts` now mirrors every type, step
count and cap within 1e-6. Schema: `RoofIntent {source, form, pitchDeg,
evidence}` on a type or placement, facts `roofSource.kind: 'front'` and
`rowClamp`, `continuity.rowCoherence`. Roof source per pand:
`roof.source` / `keepSurvey` / else `front` when a street front is gabled
or has `measuredEavesM` (strip or row); cornice fronts keep the face
rule (a first cut made wide-capped cornices flat but z-fought the De
Clercqstraat Amsterdam School neighbours' coplanar roofs and 3DBAG shows
1.5 m of roof behind those parapets, so it was dropped; `roof.form:
flat` per placement is the explicit way). Front forms
(`recipeRoof.ts saddleUnderProfile`, `FrontRoofSpec` per band): a saddle
under the crown outline (ridge at the band centre, 3 cm under every
outline vertex, 30–65°); an attic face behind dormers or a `frontRoof`
hint; otherwise a 3DBAG-bounded attic that goes flat when p95 < eaves +
1 m; when the crown spans only part of the front (side eaves would drop
> 1 m) an attic with the reason reported. Gates: front `height-vs-3dbag`
roofMax ≤ max(band lines, crown-outline tops) + 0.3 m (dormers + 1.9)
and ≥ eaves; new `roof-under-crown` (facade line every 0.1 m, 5 mm
inside, roof ≤ outline + 3 cm). Row coherence (`rowCoherence.ts`): rows
= consecutive same `type.type`, builtYear ± 2 of the modal, ≥ 3 members;
the line is the strip median when ≥ half the members are strip-measured,
else the mode of the unmeasured members' 3DBAG eaves (densest 0.4 m
window, and of windows ≥ 70 % as dense the lowest, since misreads are
upward; single linkage had chained 315-359's cornice readings into the
flat-top readings), mean-shift refined; sub-rows of ≥ 3 adjacent members
within 0.15 m keep their own line (222-228 vs 212-220; a pair is not
enough, 319/321 are two adjacent misreads); clamp > 0.8 m off unless
strip-measured or skyline-confirmed → `measuredEavesM` per front and
`facts.rowClamp`; roofMax > row ridge + 0.2 → capped at ridge + 0.1.
`stepsFromFlanks`: round(mean(L, R)), max when exactly one flank's
coverage < 0.7 (`PhotoGable.flankCoverage`). Golden (46 faces, 371

## The overview-to-city switch is a blend: worst step 70 % → 2 % of pixels over ΔE 20 (2026-10-16)

Lane `lane/overview-transition-20261016` (b91c77955), answering "the
transition from the map-coloured flat overview to our shaded city is
jarring". `src/canalRecall/overviewTransition/blend.ts` defines one blend
value, 0 at map zoom 14 and 1 at 15.6 on a smooth S-curve, with
hysteresis for whether the city draws at all (on above 0.02, off below
0.005); `?transition=0` or `window.__canalRecallTransition = false`
restores the old hard switches exactly. Basemap: the own-ground palette
at every zoom, not only under resident cells; `basemapOverview.ts` gives
the map's protected areas the land tone (the UNESCO canal belt had
turned the Grachtengordel green) and the flat footprints the city's roof
tone (`CITY_ROOF`), kept until 16.2 instead of ending at 14 (that
cut-off was a ΔL −28 jump of its own). Own ground fades in with real
alpha over the first 40 % of the blend while still flat-coloured (a
screen-door dither re-randomised under the moving camera, ~6 % sparkle
per step, rejected), opaque once in, its lit textured colour mixing in by
the blend. Buildings appear in the footprint tone and take their own
colour across the window (`cityTone`/`cityFlat` uniforms in both
shaders). Shadow intensity scales with the blend (`SharedFrame`
`shadowRamp`) instead of switching on at zoom 15; the dark footprint
raster of the overview is gone by 14. Nothing renders twice. Measured
(desktop 1280×800, chase, flight from 0.15× driving zoom over 1.9 s):
before, the switch step at z15 moved 80.7 % (Westerstraat) and 83.0 %
(Kinkerstraat) of pixels over ΔE 20 with whole-frame median ΔL −86 and
−91; camera motion alone moves 40–46 % between 100 ms frames, so the
switch is measured by a straight-down 0.1-zoom sweep with motion
cancelled: worst step 69.7 % / 69.3 % before, 2.4 % / 2.0 % after (at
15.5 → 15.6), worst Δ mean luma −3.8 / −5.2, sweep floor 0.3–1 %; phone
(not asserted) worst 4.7 % at 13.9 → 14. `vector-map.js` edits: ~282
`shadowRamp`, ~645–648 overview raster opacity, ~2054 palette patches
re-applied after the own ground loads, ~2106–2125 patches in
`_setBasemapGroundHidden`. Tests: `look/overviewTransition.test.ts` (7,
under `test:look`), `tests/e2e/overview-transition.spec.ts` (desktop: ≤
5 % of pixels over ΔE 20 and |Δ mean luma| ≤ 10 per step; `TRANSITION_AB=1`
proves `?transition=0` fails the bound); ride-perf unchanged (16.7 ms
frames, map 2.4 ms, three.js 0.8 ms, no frame over 50 ms).
`scripts/look/transition-zoom.ts` captures and builds the strips
`docs/images/look/transition-{before,after}.jpg`. Open: the flat overview
now uses the city's colours with roof-toned footprints and reads darker
and browner than the old white-and-blue map (the user decides whether it
still reads as a map); far from the rider the map's footprints fade out
where no 3D buildings are streamed (before they popped); in a tilted
manual zoom-out walls appear in the footprint tone through a short
dither; the tones come from `groundPalette(groundLookFrom())` and
`CITY_ROOF` and should switch to the sunny look's `sceneTokens()`.

## Sloterplas galerijflats as one instanced type; building-type far boxes restored under the shared frame (2026-10-16)

User asked where the "big buildings" by the Sloterplas stood in the
modelling queue (they were #1,101-1,113 of 1,828 in the dominant-building
backlog by footprint / distance) and agreed the repetition made them
worth a type. Lane `lane/sloterplas-towers-20261016` (ed25a546c kit,
4498af481 staged area; installed in 3734cf7b1): BAG panden
0363100012095578 / 063809 / 151987, Burgemeester Hogguerstraat 1-1223,
built 1965, 190 dwellings + 25 garages each (BAG via api.data.amsterdam.nl;
architect not found in an open source, not claimed). One design
(`nw-gallery-slab-15st-hogguer`), two units: 063809's west entrance wing is
22 m instead of 13 m (`long-entrance`). The small panden 0363100012196327
(north end bay) and 0363100012201815 (entrance wing) are absorbed and
suppressed through a new `alsoSuppress` on the instance. Generator
extensions, byte-identical for all 32 earlier types: `insetM` walls inside
the gallery/balcony footprint, a `gallery` element, `span`/`repeat`,
`frameStyle: 'strips'`, `annexes` (garage row on a 3.48 m pitch, lift
tower, open stairs, entrances), `bodyFromRoof` (the BAG ring includes the
garages; the slab body comes from the 3DBAG roof), flat types ignore 3DBAG
ridges, sheets lit with the sun at each panorama's own time. Measured:
body 109.5 x 12.3-12.6 m, 15 storeys at 2.92 m, 5.5 m module; parapets
#e9e8d9, panels #d8d5ca, lift brick #b6a38a, garage doors #67262a.
23.4k tris and ~410 KB per unit; 777 KB for all three.

Integration found that **every building-type far instance was a hole in
the default game**. Own ground (default since 2026-10-14) implies the
shared frame, whose recipe look is `MeshLambertMaterial`; the runtime's
`isRecipe` only accepted the unlit `ShaderMaterial`, so no unit merged and
the far box (built only from mergeable materials) was never made, while
the far pands' extrusions stayed suppressed: past 140 m all 3,072
Nieuw-West instances drew nothing. Fix in `runtime.ts`: a unit that cannot
merge gets its far box as two instanced meshes in its own lit wall/roof
materials (unit test fails without it). The near limit now scales with
the unit (`nearMetresFor`: max(140, 3 x max(length, eaves)) - only these
slabs change, to 329 m), so the three towers stay detailed across the
lake instead of turning into grey boxes. In-game (`building-types-runtime`
views `sloterplas-galleries|lake|close`): all three near, 22 draws, 70k
tris, frame median 16.7 ms desktop and iPhone at 4x. The shared-frame near
path is still unmerged (one draw per material per unit), see TODO.

gesloten verharding → paving; `erf` by vegetated share ≥ 0.5 lawn, ≥ 0.25

(`cells.json` with provenance, 226 of 294 cells, 3.5 MB gz total, median

draw into the park surface layers with the land under them hidden and

ground inside blocks from the Bloemgracht to the Tuinstraat and the
Lijnbaansgracht to the Keizersgracht read 64 % vegetated, 28 % paving, 6
% bare with courtyards against 2 % vegetated, 95 % bare without (test
bounds > 40 % and < 5 %); four unit tests (mapping, pixel test, interior
test, a drawn lawn hiding the land); `check:own-ground-cells` no FAIL,

scratchpad, not committed; rebuild with `add-bgt-courtyards.ts --raw
<dir>`, review the report, then `--publish`. Frame
`docs/images/ride-review-20261014/fix-J4-courtyards.jpg`; doc

yard reads as lawn (one 2025 flight from above); the 1,711 shadowed
yards stay bare; sheds show as holes; fences and BGT vegetation objects
are not drawn; roof gardens excluded; blocks open on more than ~3 of 16

## Sunny look is the default: measured exposure, white-balanced rig, measured clear sky (2026-10-16)

Lane `worktree-agent-a2d8e28de68096908` (b9c4b8126), answering "the game
feels a little dark/dour"; `?look=legacy` opts out. Rig
(`rendererShared/lightRig.ts`): sun `#ffe2bf` (was `#ffe9cc`); fill is the
measured clear sky mixed toward white until flat ground in sun gets
neutral light (`#b5d2ea`; the pure sky colour turned every warm brick grey
and was rejected); ground bounce from the orthophoto's sunlit pavement;
sky intensity keeps the 0.41 shade-to-sun wall ratio; sun direction and
shadows unchanged. Exposure 1.423 = 1 / (light on a sun-facing wall), so
a wall facing the sun draws its own colour (the old rig drew it at 0.74),
folded into the light intensities instead of tone mapping so the route
ribbon, question street and highlight keep exact colours; the ground gain
follows the rig (1.208 → 0.996). Sky: MapLibre's sky is the clear sky
measured from 300 clear views out of 1,256 municipal panoramas (`#9ec3ed`
upper, `#a1c6e5` at the roofline; before, the basemap land colour showed
above the horizon as cream). Measured walls with a recorded white are
scaled in linear light by sunlit white (219, median light-trim white of
the 35 May–September crops) ÷ the crop's recorded white, one factor for
all channels (148 crops across 106 houses in `measuredWhitePoints.ts`),
else the median correction 1.106, bounded 0.85–1.6, in both the city-look
and recipe-house paths. Tokens: `look/sunny.ts` exports `sceneTokens()`
and `groundTokens()`; `basemapGroundPatches` reads `groundTokens`, so the
flat overview and the 3D ground share values (unit-tested). Before →
after median luma/chroma: walls +9–15 luma, −1 to −6 chroma (cooler shade
sides, warm sun sides), e.g. Kinkerstraat 100/30 → 115/27 (ΔE 6.5), Jan
Evertsenstraat 65/29 → 74/26, Prinsengracht 94/24 → 106/23; roofs +7–12;
paved ground within ±2 luma except Singelgracht +10, chroma −6 to −9
because cast shadows are sky-blue; water within 2; sky 239/15 → 190/79

## roads-v1: the surveyed BGT road partition fetched city-wide, seven pilot cells published (2026-10-16)

Lane `lane/roads-data-20261016` (d8f734147 scripts and schema, 1670a1b9b
pilot publish; plan `docs/plans/road-surfaces-roof-rules-20261016.md`
Part 1). `scripts/own-ground/fetch-bgt-roads.ts` pulls PDOK BGT
`wegdeel` per cell with a 30 m pad and `datetime=<today>` (without it
the API returns history), keeping lokaal_id, functie, fysiek_voorkomen,
plus_fysiek_voorkomen, relatieve_hoogteligging, status, eind_registratie
and bronhouder: 294 cells, 267,614 features, pilot 104 s, city 522 s at
concurrency 6. `build-bgt-roads.ts` dedupes by lokaal_id, drops
spoorbaan (1,812), ruiterpad, airfield and h < 0 (200), classes by
`classOf`, meshes carriage/parking/driveway by fysiek_voorkomen (open →
klinker, gesloten → asphalt, half → gravel), foot/pedestrian → paving,
cycle → cycle, with the `isFietsstraat` override limited to carriageway
highways and stations 6 m from way ends (it first turned 150 junction
polygons red under Overtoom/Rokin from red-asphalt cycleways); kerbs are
shared edges between carriage/parking/cycle and foot/pedestrian at equal
h (exact 1e-7° hash; all pilot cells are bronhouder G0363); `coverWays`
are OSM ways with ≥ 80 % of their 2 m stations inside compatible
polygons. Cell schema `{version, key, surfaces: [{k, c, h, r}], kerbs,
coverWays}` typed and validated in `ownGround/roadCells.ts`
(`roadCellProblems`, `ROAD_CELL_BUDGET_GZ`, `ROADS_TOTAL_BUDGET_GZ`;
`test:roads-cells` 7/7 validates every published cell, kerb vertices
within 0.3 m of a boundary for ≥ 97 %). Pilot (-3_-1, -2_-1, -3_0, -2_0,
-1_-1, -1_0, -2_1): 16,223 polygons (foot 6,107, parking 5,213, carriage
3,287, cycle 864, driveway 669, pedestrian 83; h=1 653), 4.08 M → 209 k
vertices at 0.1 m, 43 B/polygon, 696 KB gz total (max 111 KB, median 99
KB against the 350 KB budget), 2,531 kerb runs, 20 carriage polygons red
from 14 fietsstraat ways, 61 h ≥ 1 polygons over no deck. Cover share:
residential 91 %, tertiary 97 %, secondary/primary 99 %, busway 94 %,
living_street 64 %, footway 56 %, cycleway 47 % (fietspad for ~60 % of
the way and crossing rijbaan for the rest, so they fail the 80 % rule),
path 36 %; overall 72 %. City-wide, staged only in source-data
(`datasets/bgt-roads-20261016/`, 257 MB raw, 10 MB staged): 223,590
polygons, 9.7 MB gz (max 115 KB, median 21 KB), 62 % of ways covered
(track, bridleway, path and service drag it down: yards and park paths
are not wegdeel), 400 h ≥ 1 polygons over no deck (75.9 ha, A10 and
western-harbour viaducts). BGT cannot say: squares, yards and park paths
(`onbegroeidterreindeel`/erf), overpasses without a registered deck,
tram beds in their own right-of-way, and klinker vs tegels (89 % of
plus_fysiek_voorkomen is null). Attribution `BGT © Kadaster (CC0 1.0)`
in cells.json.

## Landmark abutter survey: buildings in a landmark's angles and walls (2026-10-16)

Lane `lane/landmark-abutters-survey-20261016` (dd7ca183c). The user saw a
4-storey stucco kit block in an angle of the Noorderkerk's Greek cross;
BAG/3DBAG and the register say the angles hold the 1623 corner houses
("dienstwoningen diagonaal tussen de armen", rijksmonument 3923) with
slanted roofs. `check:osm-under-models` could not see it: it flags only
city buildings at least 50 % inside a model footprint, and the corner
houses are outside it. New typed module `landmarkAbutters.ts` (8 tests)
lists unsuppressed city buildings that share a wall with a placed model
(measured edge length, corner touches excluded), sit mostly inside its
convex hull (angle/notch/courtyard), or overlap it below 50 %, and scores
them on bouwjaar, shared monument record, shared address, 3DBAG roof vs
the drawn roof, hull position and wall length; terrace damping (-1.5)
for one-sided walls outside the hull, and a "wraps" bonus only with walls
on two sides. 337 landmarks, 560 candidates (526 wall, 133 notch, 166
partial); 95 photo-reviewed (all 43 notch candidates at score >= 8, top
25 overall, up to 3 per church): 25 fold-in, 4 separate-but-wrong, 53
fine, 13 unclear. Clearest true signal: OSM building parts on the
church's own pand (Oude Kerk, Sint Nicolaas, Noorderkerk); next, a
slanted 3DBAG roof under an OSM flat box. False positives: terraced
fronts of a block the landmark wraps, complex-wide monument records,
same-era streets, convex hulls of large irregular models (RAI, Centraal,
Rijksmuseum, Heineken). Gate `check:landmark-abutters` (in `check:canal`)
fails on any unreviewed notch candidate at score >= 8; reviews and
PENDING fold-ins live in `landmark-abutters-allowlist.json` with pano ids
and crop paths. Contact sheets were kept outside the repo in
`map-recall2-worktrees/landmark-abutters-sheets-20261016/`. Queue in TODO P2.

## Ride review, Jordaan and Plantage: three fixes, seventeen rows (2026-10-14)

Lane `lane/ride-review-jordaan-plantage-20261014`. New
`scripts/ride-review-shots.mjs` runs one seeded ride in chase view at
1280×800, holding the pose every 60 m, at turns over 25°, 35 m before each
routed bridge and at named landmarks, quiz cards visible; specs in
`scripts/ride-review/`; every frame viewed in 2×2 grids at 640 px, suspects
at full size (`docs/images/ride-review-20261014/{jordaan,plantage}-contact.jpg`,
doc `docs/ride-review-jordaan-plantage-20261014.md`). **Fixes:** (1) movable
leaves get their fixed spans: the Nijlpaardenbrug BRU1907 was a 10 m leaf
floating mid-canal with the cycleway cut at both quays, because the
register footprint of a movable bridge is the leaf only while the OSM way
runs 36 m quay to quay; `movableApproaches` in `decks.ts` extends the leaf
along each OSM bridge way through it (leaf width, at most 30 m a side),
`groundStore.cellInput` adds these spans as flat decks exempt from the
water cut on street bands, the portal stays on the leaf; named regression
BRU1907 in `check:own-ground-cells` (deck and cycle band at 0.2/0.3/0.7/0.8
of the way). (2) Landmark roof wash uses the frame's up: with the
Westertoren card open the whole Westerkerk turned orange, walls included,
because the highlight passed up = +y which is north in the shared frame;
`LANDMARK_WORLD_UP` in `look/highlight.ts` (+z in the shared frame, +y in
the older paths), measured up vector [-0.06, 0, -1] → [0, 1, 0]; `test:look`
reproduces the chain. (3) Zoos are green: the city fetch never queried
`tourism=zoo`, so Artis read as a sand plaza; `areaKind` maps zoo to park,
`fetch-osm-ground.ts` queries it, `scripts/own-ground/add-zoo-areas.ts`
(osmium from the cached extract) added 16 zoo polygons to 15 published
cells (Artis plus 15 petting farms, 19.8 ha); turning Artis green exposed
bare land through the green in hollows (14 % of Artis, 54 % of its west
third in the next cell), so `groundCell` skips land squares wholly inside
a park-class area of the cell or its neighbours (small risk of a gap at
the far ring's coarser neighbour; none seen at Wertheimpark or the
Hortus); named regression a8733446 (3 % bare land over 72 probes, 53 %
without the zoo). **Open rows** (place as lng, lat, bearing): Jordaan J2
the Westerkerk roofs still get the small-target wash though the church
fills ~15 % of the frame (the marker measures the boost on the tower
footprint); J3 the Westertoren is out of frame until ~100 m (chase pitch);
J4 inner-block gardens draw as bare sand, blocks read as squares (no OSM
area, default land); J5 Bloemgracht houses at 30–60 m are flat grey boxes
(streamed tier); J6 grey slabs over the four corners of the
Nieuwe-Wercksbrug BRU0063 (deck top 4–10 m onto land, wider than the
street bands); J7 playground slabs and a white frame float on the
Noordermarkt; J8 the Egelantiersgracht mouth looks closed (Pansemertbrug
BRU0124 a flush 8.4 m deck). Plantage P3 the Entrepotdok warehouses are
long dark boxes with khaki roofs and loose gable stubs; P4 the Walter
Süskindbrug BRU0237 reads as a thin white wire cube (movable without deck
data drawn as posts and beam); P5 no Artis main gate; P6 the Hollandsche
Schouwburg is an ordinary terrace front; P7 dark-brown windowless masses
across from Artis; P8 a pale facade ripples along a curved footprint
(unchecked); P9 the Mahatma Gandhiplantsoen sits on a ~1 m hedge box.

## Bridge regressions on main were two readings, not the bridges (2026-10-14)

Lane `lane/bridge-regressions-20261014`. After the bridges merge met the
houseboat berths on main, `check:own-ground-belt` reported a NEW finding
at the Westerdok and the bridge-fidelity e2e failed on the Torensluis
hump; both branches had passed alone. **Belt audit:** `moorings.ts`
re-cuts shores near a boat into collinear 0.5 m pieces and the audit
took at least one sample per segment, so the reviewed Westerdok spot
went from 16 to 106 samples and its worst sample moved 1.4 m off its
KNOWN key; with berths off the old audit reproduced the lane's "7
findings, all KNOWN" exactly. Fix in `ownGround/roadRegressions.ts`:
`shoreSamples` joins collinear pieces back into one segment before
sampling every 5 m (identical output without berths), and reviewed quay
spots match a finding within 15 m (`KNOWN_SPOT_M`, `spotDistanceM`) in
`scripts/own-ground/audit-belt.ts`; one real new KNOWN entry,
`quay-flooded:4.90768,52.38468` (ground −2.05 under the default −1.77
plane on the IJ-side dock quay; a berth cut moved a sample onto it).
**Torensluis hump:** deck body, deck top and quay walls are byte-identical
between the lane tip and main (cell build hashed); the e2e took the hump
from single columns, so on the lane the 28 px came from a railing post
against the next bridge down the Singel, and on main an orange-outlined
figure on the crown and streaks at the deck ends tipped the reading to
−12 px. Fix in `own-ground-bridge-fidelity.spec.ts`: `spanColumns`
projects the deck-span ends to screen columns and `readMask` takes the
median top edge over column bands between them, ignoring mask runs under
6 px, so posts, rails, figures and neighbouring bridges no longer decide
it (Seven Bridges 138 px, BRU0073 94, BRU0038 11; the lane's 296 was
also an artefact; the Torensluis reads 4.5–5.5 px against a threshold of
