## Ground from the terrain everywhere, with a reach test: 312 pands corrected, 98 split-level pands restored (2026-10-14)

Lane `lane/ground-rule-everywhere-20261014`, the follow-up to "3DBAG
ground outliers". One helper, `pandGroundNap(attributes, terrainAt,
ringRd)` in `bag3dCityJson.ts`, samples the terrain under and around a
footprint and applies `trustedGroundNap`; every reader goes through it:
`readBagBuildings`, `buildingRecipe/facts.ts` (`buildFacts` with
`terrainAt`, `heights.groundSource: 'terrain'` only when used, so
ordinary facts are byte-identical; `regroundFacts` / `trustFactsGround`
for committed facts, used by the recipe compile and large-tier CLIs),
`blockFace/compile.ts` (`faceFactsOnTrustedGround`; the front-roof
re-pitch and shell-top lines read `heights.groundNAP`),
`streetChunks/ground.ts` (`planGround` trusts each house before the
median), `buildingTypes/facts.ts` (`paramsFromFacts` returns
`groundNapM`, `build.ts` places houses on it), and
`facade/sources/netherlands.ts` (pure `bag3dPands` +
`bag3dMassingRecords`, `fetchMassing({terrainAt})`); CLIs inject
`sharedTerrain()` from `scripts/lib/terrainField.ts`. **The rule change:**
the first rule had false positives, among them the main pand of four
recipes (Stadsloket West, Politie West Overtoomsesluis, Volewijkshof 6,
Westerdoksdijk 9): the AHN terrain under a footprint is interpolated
across the building's gap, so a pand on split-level ground (a raised
deck, a dike, a quay) reads the high side (Stadsloket West: 3DBAG ground
+0.82 NAP on the A10 side street, terrain under it +4.70 from the Bos en
Lommerplein deck, +0.71 four metres outside the walls). Measured across
the 410 replaced pands (lowest terrain 4 m outside the walls minus
3DBAG's ground): 98 within 1.5 m (median ground −0.26 NAP, one on a
fallback value), 4 between 1.5 and 2 m, the rest 2–12 m with 111 on the
shared fallback values. `GROUND_REACH_M = 1.5`: 3DBAG's ground is kept
when the terrain just outside the walls comes within 1.5 m of it; 312
pands stay on the terrain (Nassaukade 63X 15.57 → 5.42 m, nearest
outside terrain +0.29 against −9.67), 98 are restored. Unit tests per
reader on Nassaukade 63X and its ordinary neighbour 0363100012207164
(fixture `fixtures/bag3d-nassaukade-63x.json` from 3DBAG v20250903),
Stadsloket West pinned as the split-level case; `streetChunks.test.ts`
is now in `test:street-rendering-core`. No golden changed: 560 committed
`facts.json` unchanged, fit-golden 153, 112 meshes, 24 face chunks all
identical. **Published data** (own commit): `fix-bag-ground-outliers.ts`
rewritten to sync tiles to the rule with staging, and
`build-bag-buildings.ts --base=` ran a true `--tiles` rebuild on the
staged building-tiles that agreed with the patch on every ground change
(building-tiles come from the OSM merge whose `buildings-osm.geojson` is
in no checkout, hence patch not full rebuild): building-tiles 66 heights
in 39 files (64 raised back +3.02..+8.27 m, median +3.35, the split-level
pands; 2 true outliers lowered −3.26 and −3.68 m that the first patch
missed because tiles 8412/5383 and 8413/5383 are one compact JSON value),
bag-tiles 73 features in 38 files, bag-facts 73 descriptors; the two
frontage-survey tiles pinned by hash rebaked, frontages and
`profiles.json` unchanged. Not published: the rebuild also fills eaves,
ridge, roof and year for five pands in 8412/5384 missing since the Jan
Evertsen re-key (earlier staleness, on the board). Frame:
`docs/images/live-play-20261014/ground-outlier-canal-before-after.jpg`,
a 5.4 m courtyard pand behind the Entrepotdok warehouses that poked above
the roofline before (no Herengracht or Keizersgracht pand among the 312
has a 5–8 m inflation; the closest were 4.1 and 3.2 m). Checks:
bag-tiles 22, tile-buildings 18, street-appearance 98, building-recipes
166, block-face 71, building-types 39, street-rendering-core 69,
osm-under-models 0.

## Nassaukade 506: the user's benchmark block in the kit; white courses on Kinkerstraat (2026-10-14, user)

Lanes `lane/nassaukade-506-20261014` and the merge lane
`lane/nassau-merge-20261014`. The user sent a Street View frame of the
terrace at Nassaukade 506 (Oud-West, the Singelgracht's west bank between
the Kinkerstraat and Bilderdijkstraat bridges) and said "this is an
example of a block I'd like to be well modeled by kit". Intake from the
city panoramas across the water and from the quay (source-data
`pand-reference-walls/`, `block-face-strips/nassau-145-152/`, the quay
photo); catalogue in `docs/nassaukade-506-20261014.md`: a shared grid
(tall ground 0–4.45 m, three storeys, heavy cornice at 14.0–15.4 m),
T-windows shrinking up the front (2.0 / 1.8 / 1.65 m), white bands at
sill and transom, eared heads with three keys, console sills, pointed
dormers; per pand 151-152 corner (6 axes, brick #6b5947, wreath
medallions), 150 painted near-black #524b3d with a timber turned balcony
stack and a stepped gable, 149 grey paint #6a685d, 148 brick #806e5e
with an iron grille, 147 black paint #615a47 with a bell mansard, 146 tan
brick #a98f76 with a white timber erker, 145 red brick #b58c6f. Six kit
components, typed in `intent.ts`, laid out in `fit.ts`, built in the
library or the new `oudWest.ts`, each tested and byte-identical when
absent (fit-golden 153 identical, all 24 face chunks sha256-identical to
main): `bands: 'painted'` with `bandHeights {sill, transom, head}` in
metres (defaults 0.14 / 0.10 / 0.17), `bandLines`, `bandStoreys` (white
stone bands cut around openings and at an erker; the sill band's top on
the lowest sill, the transom band centred at 0.78 of the window, the
head band on the heads); `windowSurround: 'eared-keystone'` (a 0.10 m
head slab running 0.12 m past each jamb, 0.13 × 0.25 m ear blocks,
`round(w/0.4)-1` keystone blocks); `windowSills: 'consoles'` (sill slab
on two 0.10 × 0.16 m consoles, skipped at balcony bays);
`balconies.style: 'timber-bracketed'` (0.14 m platform 0.75 m deep on
profile brackets every 1.1 m, 1.0 m guard; `rail: 'turned'` balusters
every 0.16 m at 12 triangles each, `rail: 'iron'` bars every 0.14 m;
`styleStoreys`, `storeyBays`; a 2 m balcony under 330 triangles);
`bayWindows.finish: 'painted'`; `wallMaterial: 'painted-brick'` (walls
carry `tintSource: 'measured'`, chunk buckets keyed `_measured`, so paint
skips the 0.3–0.6 lightness clamp); plus the BAG erker chord
(`blockFace/bayOutline.ts`, `intake --bay-outline=`: BAG draws 146 with
its erker in the footprint, a 1.61 m front; the chord rebuilds it to
6.17 m) and `mirrorFront` mirroring `storeyBays`. Face
`nassau-145-152` (two library types `nassau-1900-three-axis` and
`nassau-1900-two-axis-balcony`, 151-152 and 150 inline), 19,441
triangles, every gate, interference OK on all six party lines, the
corner on a recipe roof at 30° (its 3DBAG shell had a 33.5 m hole);
compiled, not installed. After the merge with the canal-windows and
Kinkerstraat keys (conflicts in `intent.ts`, `fit.ts`, `fitLarge.ts`
resolved as the union: `WINDOW_SURROUNDS` with `sill` and
`eared-keystone`, `bands` with `courses`, `speklagen` and `painted`, the
eared early-out before the sill/keystone/lintel chain, console sills
after the keystone block, `measuredSlots` dedupe with the painted-brick
material map) the face got `windows: 't-window'`, window heights as
shares of the catalogue storey grid `[0.6, 0.57, 0.55, 0.59]` (the canal
survey's `'diminishing'` medians 0.72–0.76 drew every window ~0.5 m too
tall on this row, which measures ~0.57), and `windowHead {kind:
'relieving', storeys: [3], archRing {stone, blocks, keystone}}` on 150 and
147. Verdict at gallery size (`docs/images/nassaukade-506/
photo-over-model.jpg`, `quay-perspective-640.jpg` at 44 m,
`four-sides.jpg`): 149 and 145 strongest, bands, eared heads, consoles
and turned balconies all match; 148 layout right, plainer grille; 147
colour and both balconies, mansard straight not bell-shaped; 146 erker
position and colour, box sides not canted; 150 gable, colour, balcony
stack, the storey-3 arches now the most visible gain; 151-152 massing,
grid, dormers. Still wrong: the photo's arches are round with dark
tympana, two springers and a keystone where the kit draws a segmental
arch with five blocks; heads sit slightly high on the common 0.86 head
line; the medallions, bracketed cornice with modillions, carved pediment
and fretwork dormers, cast-iron grilles, the bell mansard, the souterrain
with side stoop, canted erker sides, shop awnings and signs. **Kinkerstraat
wiring:** `kinker-1895-painted-band`'s black-painted palette switched from
the stucco slot to `wallMaterial: 'painted-brick'` (Kinkerstraat 28 now
#535955 against the photo's #5e645d); `kinker-1890-brick-arched` got
`bands: 'painted', bandLines: ['sill','transom'], bandHeights {sill:
0.1, transom: 0.12}` (the 0.04 / 0.05 m first proposed drew lines under
2 px at 40 px/m, and the default head line sat on the arch springing
~0.75 m above the photo's course; the type's evidence measures the rows
at 0.10–0.13 m); kinker-2-30 recompiled 28,695 → 32,043 triangles, the
sill course on the photo's sill line, the upper course ~0.3 m above the
photo's (the photo's sits at ~0.63 of the window height, the kit fixes
the transom at 0.78), both courses grey stone where the photo's are

kit (memory `nassaukade-506-benchmark`).

## Ground tones measured from the orthophoto; `bright` is the ground look; measured glass keeps the sky (2026-10-14, user)

**Ground look** (lane `lane/ground-look-20261014`, user "city too
dark" after the first light pass). Real Amsterdam ground tones measured
on the PDOK 8 cm orthophoto (126 tiles, sampled on the own-ground OSM
band labels over the Singelgracht, Houtmankade and Prinsengracht, label
noise and tree crowns dropped, the aerial's blue haze subtracted in
linear light, sun and shadow split per surface;
`scripts/own-ground/measure-ground-tones.ts`,
`docs/ground-tones-20261014.md`): sunlit asphalt 168,166,157 (luma 166),
pavement 172,164,151 (165), klinker 160,146,135 (148), cycle red
185,165,151 (168), canal water seen from above 50,55,55 (54). So from
above the ground is bright and nearly one lightness and the legend lives
in hue; and today's default missed the legend bar (asphalt/klinker ΔE
18.5). Three palettes in `ownGround/groundLook.ts` behind `?groundLook=`:
`measured` (the orthophoto values with brick and cycle red saturated to
clear ΔE 20), `bright` (road 130, pavement 175, grey-green canal 118),
`legacy-ish` (road 200, pavement 215, pale water 170); `gameGround.ts`,
`groundWorker.ts`, `farRing.ts` and `basemapPalette.ts` take their
colours from the look; paint, rails, bollards, parks, trees and facades
unchanged; the old palette byte-identical as `default`. Luma at the
Singelgracht boat spot (scene / road / pavement / water): default 131 /
110 / 144 / 105; measured 130 / 169 / 153 / 57; bright 139 / 145 / 156 /
119; legacy-ish 157 / 199 / 163 / 170; the legacy basemap 176 / 240 /
223 / 187; facades identical across looks. Verdict at gallery size:
`measured` is the data but fails as a look (streets and pavements one
beige, the canal a black slot); `legacy-ish` washes out (cycle red
candy-pink, the corridor loses contrast); `bright` keeps grey-green
water, mid-grey roads against pale pavements, red cycle tracks and the
brick quay distinct, and fixes the asphalt/brick ΔE. Integrator decision:
`bright` is the default (`GROUND_LOOK_DEFAULT`), `?groundLook=default`
gives the old palette; if it should be lighter still, the lane's next
step is bright with the road at ~150 and a deeper cycle red (~190,96,92
instead of the slightly salmon 204,107,106). Note: this lane stopped its
dev server with a pattern kill that took every worktree's server with it;
lanes now stop only the PID they started.
**Measured glass keeps the sky** (lane `lane/measured-glass-sky-20261014`,
user: "old seems better for glass? lighter?" on the Waagdragerhof row of
the measured-pilots sheet). A crop's glass colour is the glass under that
sky, not a material; drawing the exact hex lost the sky-lit pane. Rule in
`look/palette.ts`: a measured pane keeps its measured hue and saturation,
its lightness is floored at the stock pane's (L = max(measured L, 0.40);
the 0.5 blend was rejected because `#3a4650` would land at L 0.335, still
darker than the unmeasured windows beside it), and the `glassTint` layer
is now the stock pane's own brightness profile in grey (top 255 with the
streak, bottom ~103, mean 158; it had been squeezed into 188–255 and drew
measured panes flatter than stock); above ~0.62 per channel the tint
scales down as a whole so the hue holds (Houthavenkade's column glass
loses 0.022 L). Apollohal's hall glass `#46545c`: 106,126,139 stock →
74,88,97 exact → 102,122,135 now; Houthavenkade's column glass `#8e9ea4`
141,157,163 → 137,152,158 with the gradient and streak visible.
Waagdragerhof itself no longer carries measured glass (the
reconciliation dropped lane C's hand `#3a4650` for the kit glass), so the
user's exact case is pinned by a unit test instead. `measureFacade.ts`
and `measure.ts` say the look does the lift; intents unchanged. Sheets:
`docs/images/look/measured-pilots.jpg` (five columns) and
`measured-glass-ride.jpg` (ride camera, before | after). Tests: look
58/58 (floor, hue and saturation held, stock contrast, the `#3a4650`
pin), fit-golden 153 identical, 112 meshes identical, Playwright
`building-look.spec.ts` 8/8 with the measured case on Apollohal and
Houthavenkade (L within −0.03..+0.09 of max(hex L, 0.40), hue within
10°). Eight bundles carry the palette change.

## 3DBAG ground outliers: 540 pands drawn 3–12 m too tall, the rule and the patch; the lock island stays; two stale tests (2026-10-14)

Lane `lane/water-anomalies-20261014`. **The grey box in the Singelgracht**
(user's live-play frames, ~4.8789, 52.3797) is a real low industrial
pand, Nassaukade 63X (`NL.IMBAG.Pand.0363100012124441`), drawn 15.6 m
tall because 3DBAG's ground (`b3_h_maaiveld`) for it is a failed estimate
of −9.67 NAP under a +5.9 NAP roof. A scan of all 273,599 cached 3DBAG
pands against the AHN terrain extract (`ground-height-v1`) shows 3DBAG
ground normally a median 0.14 m below the terrain, but 540 pands more than
3 m below it, bunched on a few repeated values (−6.36, −6.46, −6.73,
−8.38, −9.67 NAP), among them canal-belt houses inflated by 5–8 m. Rule
`trustedGroundNap` in `src/canalRecall/bag3dCityJson.ts`: when 3DBAG's
ground is more than `GROUND_OUTLIER_M` = 3 m below the AHN terrain under
the footprint, the height is measured from the terrain; 3DBAG's ground
is kept for pands built after 2021 (after the AHN4 survey), where the
roof would clear the terrain by under 2 m (sunken pands), and where there
is no terrain sample; the LoD1.2 volume fallback is skipped when the
ground is replaced. `readBagBuildings(city, terrainAt?)`, new
`scripts/lib/terrainField.ts`, `build-bag-buildings.ts` passes the
terrain. `scripts/fix-bag-ground-outliers.ts` writes the report and with
`--publish` patched the published tiles in place: 410 pands, 363
building-tile heights, 369 bag-tile heights/eaves/ridges and 369 facts
descriptors across 184 files, heights down 3.0–12.5 m (median 5.0);
Nassaukade 63X 15.57 → 5.42 m. The frontage survey pins three of those
tiles by hash, rebaked, `profiles.json` byte-identical. Tests in
`test:bag-tiles` (19/19): the outlier replaced, plausible/newer/sunken
grounds kept, the published tile carries the re-measured height. Not yet
on the rule: `buildingRecipe/facts.ts`, `blockFace/compile.ts`,
`buildingTypes/facts.ts`, `streetChunks/ground.ts`,
`facade/sources/netherlands.ts` read `b3_h_maaiveld` directly (board).
**The Westerkanaal land blob** (~4.8839, 52.3876) is the middle head of
the Westerkanaalschutsluis lock (OSM w797542031 / w1308281538, a ~75 m²
island in water multipolygon r1142453 that the OpenFreeMap snapshot
keeps; the PDOK aerial shows the concrete head with lamps between the two
passages), not a BGT feature or a berth artefact; pinned as a regression
in `test:own-ground` (71/71) with and without berths; the kit cannot show
the lock gates or the catwalk. **Two tests red since before 2026-10-14:**
`audit-frontages.test.ts` was stale (the retired Jan Evertsen profile
left its paths and a since re-keyed tile in the survey; re-recorded with
`bake-frontages.ts`, 80 → 70 paths, frontages byte-identical,
`test:street-appearance` 98/98); the pyramid case in
`surveyedEnvelopeTransport.test.ts` had a broken harness (it stripped
only the first `import` of `pyramidal-roofs-source.js` before loading it
in a VM; a second import and a `THREE.Scene` added in 1c78b5a5 threw a
SyntaxError before any assertion; it now strips every import and stubs
`Scene`, 8/8). Frames in `docs/images/live-play-20261014/anomaly-*.jpg`.

## Statue batch 1: one command, 13 statues, five beat the kit, none shipped (2026-10-14)

Lane `lane/sculpture-batch-20261014` (plan Part 4, route B). `node
--import tsx scripts/sculptures/reconstruct.ts --id=<statue>` does photo
pick → cut-out (IS-Net fallback) → TripoSR → decimate → strip in one go:
defaults per statue in `scripts/sculptures/batch1.json` (kit model,
Commons title, height, facing); `--title="File:..."` fetches author and
licence from the Commons API and refuses anything but CC0, PD, CC BY and
CC BY-SA (`--photo` + `--page-url`/`--author`/`--licence` for other
sources); `--rembg`, `--box`, `--kit-plinth` + `--plinth-top`,
`--height`, `--facing`, `--material=bronze|stone`. Output under
`artifacts/sculpture-reconstruction/<id>/` (routeB.glb with the kit's
own bronze/stone material slots and no baked photo colour, compare.png,
source.json with URL, author, licence, date, cut-out model, timings);
`scripts/sculptures/setup-env.sh` recreates the venvs and the TripoSR
checkout; the photo cache is now keyed by the photo's sha1 (it was keyed
by id and silently reused an old photo). Results (strips in
`docs/images/sculptures/<id>.jpg`, 15–64 s each, 6k tris): better than
the kit as they stand: De Dokwerker, Mama Baranka, Waterdraagster
(Bellamyplein), Spinoza, Theo Thijssen's man; Gandhi has the better
figure but a half-height plinth with flowers baked in; need a second
photo: Anne Frank (Merwedeplein; tiny photo behind flowers), Multatuli
(night shot), Wilhelmina (side view reads, front merges), Rembrandt
(only a 19th-century print; the kit id is the Night Watch group);
worse, keep the kit: Winkler Prins (a stack of discs comes out as a
twisted stick), Walraven van Hall (a 10 m fallen tree, wrong class),
Theo Thijssen's boy (boy, desk and legs fuse); skipped: Carmiggelt (the
licensed Anefo photos show the sculptor and the widow, not the bust).
Multi-photo (the TRELLIS.2 route from the tools survey,
`scripts/sculptures/multiview/run-multi-statue.sh`): only Mama Baranka
had three licensed side views (Ceescamel (1), (3), (5)); 7 min on the MLX
port, one coherent body with real sides and back, base disc lost, strip
unshaded (no material tag in the trial); Waterdraagster, Wilhelmina
(three RCE photos) and Spinoza are the next candidates at ~7 min and
27 GB each. Nothing is installed: no catalogue entry, no
`signature-landmarks.json`, nothing under `public/`; the rule since the
user's review is that no statue ships without the user's look, so the
strips are on the demo page for a pick. Caveats: Commons rate-limits
`upload.wikimedia.org` after ~10 downloads (the fetch backs off up to
10 min); `--kit-plinth` also pulls in any kit triangle under `plinthTop`
within 1.8 m; the Theo man and boy are separate GLBs on the kit block and
need hand placement. Doc section "Batch 1" in
`docs/sculpture-reconstruction-20261014.md`.

## Multi-view tools: TRELLIS.2 with four photos gives the statue a back (2026-10-14, user)

Lane `lane/multiview-tools-20261014`, from the user's questions ("tripoSR,
could we get it to use multiple photos?", TRELLIS.2, trellis-mac,
trellis2-apple). Survey of 17 tools in
`docs/multiview-reconstruction-survey-20261014.md` (multi-image support,
licence, runs on this Mac): TRELLIS v1 is multi-image but CUDA-only;
TRELLIS.2-4B is single-image upstream with two gated helpers (DINOv3,
manual approval; RMBG-2.0, CC BY-NC); the two Apple ports run (trellis-mac
on MPS, trellis2-apple on MLX) but neither takes several images; Hunyuan3D
still excludes the EU; SAM 3D needs a 32 GB NVIDIA box; VGGT and π³
weights are CC BY-NC, MapAnything's Apache. Trial on De Dokwerker
(`docs/images/sculptures/de-dokwerker-tools.jpg`, rows kit | TripoSR |
TRELLIS.2 one photo on both ports | TRELLIS.2 four photos on both ports |
VGGT | MapAnything): the lane re-added TRELLIS v1's multi-image method to
both ports (stochastic: one photo per sampling step; multidiffusion:
every step averages all photos), converted timm's ungated DINOv3 copy
(matches to 4.9e-6; allowed under Meta's DINOv3 licence) and skipped
RMBG by feeding cut-outs. One photo: 2.7 min on MPS, 2 min on MLX, a
holed figure with detached forearms, no better than TripoSR's 20 s. Nine
images stochastic did not converge. Four Commons photos (0/90/180/−90°)
multidiffusion: 9.5 min MPS, 7 min MLX (26.7 GB), head, arms and legs
coherent from every side: the first statue whose sides and back come
from photographs. VGGT on 50° panorama crops registers to 0.9 m / 0.46°
and measures the height at 4.3 m (kit 4.13 m) but gives a lumpy front
relief; MapAnything a blob; tight telephoto crops fail to register. No
panorama is within 25 m of De Dokwerker and all stand west of the
square (front ±35°), so panoramas measure height and position, never
shape. Route: single figures with 3–4 side photos → TRELLIS.2
multidiffusion on the MLX port; TripoSR stays the one-photo fallback;
groups one run per figure; abstract and lettered memorials stay kit
primitives. trellis2-apple needed `--no-build-isolation`, a C++20 flag
and the Eigen submodule in a private copy; its Metal packages want the
Xcode Metal Toolchain (not installed, user's call); the MLX path runs
without them. Tools, venvs and 17 GB of weights in
`~/Code/map-recall2-sculpt/mv/`, outside the repo.
`decimate_scale_glb.py` gained welding, fragment filtering, `--remesh`
and `--plinth`. The batch lane was switched to this route.

## Live play at the Singelgracht: road paint, light, near detail, the brick quay, houseboat berths (2026-10-14, user)

Three lanes (`lane/live-play-20261014`, `-light-`, `-detail-`) from the
user's screenshots on the first own-ground rides, each with before/after
frames in `docs/images/live-play-20261014/` and on the demo page.
**Road paint** ("road painting in ownground still not there"): the
cross-sections drew lane lines and zebras but nothing at junctions, so
painted cycle lanes stopped at the junction edge, no arm had a stop line
or give-way teeth, cycle paths left a bare gap across side streets, and
0.10–0.12 m lines broke into specks from the chase camera. (The premise
that the legacy MapLibre ground painted markings was wrong: it paints
none.) New `ownGround/roadMarkings.ts`, wired into `streets.ts`, near ring
only, everything read from the ways because the extract has no node
tags: stop lines at signalised junctions (a `crossing=traffic_signals`
or `crossing:signals=yes` node within 30 m, behind any mapped crossing),
give-way teeth on lower-class arms (not exits, woonerven, bus/tram ways),
cycle lanes carried through the junction in red with block markings
where a side road opens, cycle-path crossings without a tag get block
markings with red between them; lines widened to 0.15 m (`PAINT_LINE_M`).
Named regression Nassaukade / Frederik Hendrikplantsoen, node
n2306196651: paint within 30 m 43 → 70 m², red 224 → 296 m²
(`test:own-ground`); e2e `own-ground-paint.spec.ts` (cockpit, `OWN_GROUND=1`)
white pixels in the junction box 0.99 % → 1.46–1.53 %, bound 1.25 %. No
bike pictograms, arrows or node-tag zebras yet (no node tags in the
extract). **Too dark**: own ground is lit by the shared frame's sun and
sky, which draws level ground at 0.83 of its palette colour (0.64 in
shadow), and the asphalt prior [72,74,78] rendered at luma 67 in sun /
59 in shade. New `ownGround/groundLight.ts`: a brightness-only gain of
1.208 on ground materials and the far ring (the sun keeps its warmth);
asphalt [86,88,93] (88 sun / 78 shade). Facades untouched (132.9 before
and after). Mean luma, boat spot: scene 108 → 116, road 81 → 99, pavement
138 → 150, water 96 → 105; the legacy basemap is 182 / 234 / 246 / 187,
so own ground is still ~60 luma below it, and that gap is now palette
(near-white legacy streets, pale water), a look decision on the board.
**Low detail from close**: facade window cells fade to their mean colour
by on-screen texels per pixel on the foreshortened vertical axis; at the
boat camera that is ~18 texels/px and the `[4, 10]` threshold assumed a
window is ~20 texels when it is ~55 × 150, so the built detail was
flattened into bands. `FACADE_TIER_FROM/TO_TEXELS` 16/30 in

Lane `lane/canal-windows-20261014`, from the user's priority ("window shape

rest had bad crops; `docs/canal-house-windows-and-accents-20261014.md`
carries every measurement and hex) gives era medians the kit had wrong:

width (old 0.51), absolute heights shrink upward (3.0 / 2.2 / 1.75 /
1.45 m on 179169), frames are white or cream on 27 of 29 fronts, a third
of the fronts are near-black painted brick (#2d2826, #303639, #3f3a33),
speklagen are 0.10–0.16 m tall every 0.45–1.1 m, arch rings 3–4 courses
or 5 blocks, quoins 0.33 m blocks at a 0.56 m pitch; window kind by era:
cross windows (17th c.), 6/8/9-over sashes (18th), six-pane, 2-over-2 and
T-windows (19th), small-pane upper sash over one pane (c.1900). New
optional keys in `intent.ts` + `fit.ts`, tested in
`streetComponents.test.ts` (10/10), byte-identical when absent
(fit-golden 140 unchanged, 107 large meshes identical): window layouts
`sash-6-over-6`, `sash-8-over-8`, `sash-9-over-9`, `six-pane`, `t-window`,
`small-over-one`, `cross-transom` (whole front or per storey via
`storeyWindows`; bars clamped 1.5 cm inside the pane); `windowHead {kind:
segmental (rise 0.08 of the width, the survey median) | round |
relieving (square window under an arch spanning width + 0.12 m), storeys,
archRing {colour stone|band|frame, style solid|blocks|none}, keystone}`;
`windowShare`; `windowHeights` per storey or `'diminishing'` (heads on a
common line at 0.86 of the storey); `storeyHeights`; `bands: 'speklagen'`
with `{spacing, courses}` (white courses 2 cm proud); `windowSurround:
'sill'`; `plinth: 'low'` (0.45 m stone); `basementBars`; `cornice:
'frieze'`. Eight surveyed houses re-fitted as `cw-*` recipes (929–2,467
tris, every gate), each with a photo | model | overlay sheet
(`docs/images/canal-windows/<id>.jpg`): Herengracht 175702 and 179665
(block arches and speklagen land on the photo's courses), Keizersgracht
176393 (bell gable, near-black) and 171052, Prinsengracht 179169
(diminishing heights) and 167765 (segmental frame heads), Herengracht
179684 (T-windows) and 176601. Fixes after looking at 640 px: segmental

## Own ground on by default; the start faces the first leg, not the snapped node (2026-10-14, user)

Lane `lane/own-ground-default-20261014`. **Own ground default** (user:
"make ownground the default"): `OWN_GROUND_DEFAULT = true` in
`vector-map.js`; `?ownGround=0` or `window.__canalRecallOwnGround = false`
turns it off, `?ownGround=1` still works, and an explicit `?sharedFrame=0`
turns it off too (the own ground draws through the shared frame) unless
`?ownGround=1` is given; `own-ground-default.spec.ts` (7/7) pins all of
that. The old `?elevation=1` stencil layer now needs `?ownGround=0`, so
`canal-elevation.spec.ts` and `CANAL_ELEVATION=1` in `ride-perf.spec.ts`
switch own ground off; `ride-perf.spec.ts` gained `OWN_GROUND=0|1`.
Desktop ride-perf on the fixed ride, medians of three runs, off → on:
frame interval 16.7/16.8/16.8 ms unchanged (locked to the display, no
long frames either way), map render 2.35 → 3.5 ms median, three.js work
0.73 → 2.11 ms per frame, JS heap 788 → 881 MB. The real cost is ~2.5 ms
of main-thread work and ~90 MB; if that headroom is needed, cut the far
ring (LOD 1 cells) first, then parks and allotments, junction rings, the
4 m relief. `index.html` bumps `vector-map.js?v=20261014-ownground` so
cached copies do not keep the old default. **Start heading** (user:
"camera starting in the wrong direction", boat at the Hugo de
Grootgracht): the planned route begins at the graph node the start was
snapped to, which can lie behind the spawn (12 m west there), and
`startHeading` measured its look-ahead from that first point, so a route
running east past the boat made the boat and the chase camera face west;
boat seed 2468ace0 and bike seed 1234abcd did the same. Fix in
`src/canalRecall/game/routeSelection.ts`: the first leg is read from the
spawn's closest point on the first ~300 m of the route (a later
near-equal segment wins so a doubled-back route reads where it passes the
spawn again; off-route spawns face the route; the road or canal direction
is kept within 30° of the leg, else the leg itself); restarts and new
rides use the same spawn code. `scripts/check-start-heading.ts` adds the
real boat and bike routes plus doubled-back, sideways and loop cases;
`start-heading.spec.ts` covers nine seeded rides and the user's start,
spawn heading and camera forward each within 30° of the first leg (11/11
desktop); `START_HEADING_OFF=old` swaps the old algorithm in and the
pinned boat start then fails. `check:canal` green on the lane. Also
found: `.cache/.cache` was a symlink to its own parent and crashed the
vite dev server with ELOOP in any worktree with a `.cache` link
(removed); and `check:canal` rebuilds nine bundles main had out of date
(building-style, building-tiles, game-landmarks, game-recall, game-ui,
notice-cards, orientation-pois, recall-store, three), rebuilt and
committed here.

## Measured glass reaches the game; the sheet's city-look column was the liar (2026-10-14)

Lane `lane/measured-look-20261014` (plan Part 1 lane B, second pass). The
two "look bugs" the kit-vocabulary sheet showed were one real and one
false. **False:** measured dark walls were never near-black in the game;
the sheet's "re-fit, city-look tints" column came from lane C's scratch
`compare.ts`, which passed trial texture tiles to `renderModels`, and that
branch of `render-page.ts` skipped the game look and drew the GLB's raw
colours under a hemisphere + sun light (Waagdragerhof's `#4a302b` tower
rendered 31,18,16 there while both game looks drew it 78,50,46, ΔL
+0.01); Houthavenkade's "pale grey" plum half was the raw reflective
glass. The trace from intent → fit slot → export extras →
`slotForMaterial` → `cityLookTint` → shader ruled out a double bypass, a
shade multiplication and a stucco/paint mis-slot. Fix: `render-page.ts`
and `render.ts` always draw through a game look (`renderModels(models,
views, {city, year})`, `--city-look [--year=]`); the `--textures` path is
retired and a texture map now throws. **Real:** `cityTint('glass')`
returned white for every glass, so `palette.glass` never reached the game.
Glass with `tintSource: 'measured'` now uses a twelfth slot layer,
`glassTint` (the pane gradient and sky streak in grey, 188–255), tinted by
`cityMeasuredGlassTint` (hex ÷ the cell's exact mean), in `palette.ts`,
`slotCells.ts`, `cityLook.ts`, `recipeLook.ts` and `writeTile.ts`; a new
layer because the old blue-grey pane's mean caps any tint below pale
reflective glass; unmeasured glass unchanged. `fitLarge` adds a measured
group's `glass@g<i>` to `measuredSlots` (not in the fit-golden hash).
Also found: measured brick in 20th-century buildings sampled the lighter
`brick20` cell and drew 0.02–0.03 L light; measured brick now always
samples the canal brick. Result on the three re-fits: every measured
wall, arch ring and glass within 0.02 L of its authored hex in both game
looks (`scripts/look/measured-walls.ts` id-pass table; e.g. Houthavenkade
glass `#8e9ea4` rendered 89,107,118 before, 141,157,163 after; Apollohal
glass `#46545c` 106,126,139 → 74,88,97). Tests: look 40/40 (measured glass
cell × tint within 1.5 per channel for six hexes; layer choice; `dress`
attributes), building-recipes 134, fit-golden 140 identical, large meshes
107 identical, tileBuildings 18/18, Playwright `building-look.spec.ts`
with a new case loading a re-fit GLB in both looks (every material within
0.05 L, the looks within 0.02 of each other); the city-look gallery review
on six installed models is pixel-identical (no installed model carries
`tintSource` yet). Atlas +1/12 (~0.5 MB at 256 px). `docs/LOOK.md` gained
"Measured colours". The re-fits still wait for the reconciliation lane
(lane A's measured values on lane C's systems) before they install.

## Hosting: auto-prune after every deploy, bursts deploy once (2026-10-14)

Deploys failed on the 10 GB Hosting quota again this morning (24 failed
runs; 521 stored versions listed, of which the finalized ones from the
last 24 hours were the 10 GB). Every push to main deploys both sites
(~190 MB canalrecall + ~100 MB edumap), 27–72 deploys a day in October,
so the quota holds about half a day. The user chose both fixes: the deploy
workflow now runs `scripts/hosting/prune-versions.mjs --keep=3 --apply`
after a successful deploy with the same service account (keeps the live
release and the newest three per site, never fails the deploy), and
`cancel-in-progress: true` so a burst of pushes deploys once. The manual
"Prune Firebase Hosting versions" workflow and `npm run hosting:prune`
stay for emergencies.

## Texture prototype: the kit wins on all three complaint houses (2026-10-14, night)

The user said to keep improving the kit and try the photo texture too, so
a lane built the texture route on the three complaint houses
(`docs/texture-prototype-20261014.md`, `docs/images/texture-prototype/`;
`scripts/building-recipes/export-textured.ts` lands with lane A's
tooling it depends on): every street-facing panel matched to its
rectified panorama crop, exposure-normalised, masked pixels (foliage,
missing, the bottom 2.5 m for vehicles) inpainted from the nearest wall
rows, posterised to 12 colours from the brick cell tones at 8 px/m, one
atlas per house, mapped through the crop-to-panel offsets, rendered beside
the installed kit and the photo at 640 px and 200 px. Verdict, the lane's
and the integrator's: kit on all three. Houthavenkade 26's texture does
show the orange/plum split the kit misses, but windows become blotches,
the bay columns smears, the ground floor repeats the storey above, and at
3/4 the wall is a billboard; Apollohal's only panorama (2017-04) is behind
trees in leaf so 62 % was inpainted; Waagdragerhof's arches, the one thing
that identifies it, become ragged blobs and the hazy panorama turns the
brick pink-grey. Textured walls skip the look's baked sun shading and read
darker and colder than kit walls on the same model. Cost: 3–6× the kit's
GPU memory uncompressed (about level with UASTC, which `toktx` was not
installed to measure), 4–9× smaller to download, 5–6 draws vs 11–14. So the
texture is not a shipping route; what it proved is which facts the kit
lacks (the colour split, the glazing fraction, the arch shape), which lane
C's vocabulary and lane A's measurement supply. Two bugs found in lane A's
tooling and sent back: `walls.json` records the requested 50 px/m even when
the rectifier lowers the scale on long walls, and the foliage test misses
spring leaves. Also: the `tileBuildings` golden was re-recorded for three
large recipes installed since (Da Costakade 146, Hirschpassage 2,
Leidsekade 106) and one changed row, De Balie (uninstalled recipe compiled
by the tile compiler, 1,307 → 1,733 tris from kit changes in the batches).

## Measured tint, the shared house-type library, the sculpture prototype, motorkade-1 restored (2026-10-14, night)

Three plan lanes merged. **Measured tint** (`lane/measured-tint-20261014`,
plan Part 1 lane B): a wall whose colour was measured from the photo now
renders at that colour. `cityWallTint`'s clamp (brick lightness 0.3–0.6,
saturation 0.12–0.5) is untouched because it protects the ~343k streamed
buildings; the bypass is the pattern the file already used for the slate
exception: the exporter writes `tintSource: 'measured'` into material
extras when `material.userData.tintSource === 'measured'` (measured and
unmeasured buckets never merge), `slotForMaterial` reads it, and
`cityMeasuredWallTint` in `palette.ts` returns the authored hex (L floored
at 0.18) divided by the brick cell mean (225/255) so cell × tint lands on
the authored colour; the same source parameter runs through `cityTint`,
`cityLookTint`, `slotTintBytes`, `dress`, `recipeLook.ts`,
`galleryReview.ts`, `render-page.ts` and `writeTile.ts` so sheets and
converted tiles match the game. Swatches through the real look: dark
`#3a2a28` rendered 79,57,54 before and 57,42,39 after; pale `#d8d2c4`
rendered tan 151,140,115 before and 213,207,193 after. Tests in
`palette.test.ts`, `cityLook.test.ts` (162 pass) and a Playwright case in
`building-look.spec.ts`; unmeasured output byte-identical (fit-golden,
large-mesh hashes). Nothing sets the flag yet; lane A's fit does.
**Shared house-type library** (`lane/type-library-20261014`, plan Part 2
step 1): `BlockFaceIntent.types` accepts ids next to inline types; a
library type is one file at `scripts/block-face/types/<district>/<id>.json`
(`HouseTypeIntent` plus `district` equal to the folder, required
`evidence`, optional `schemaLimits`); `blockFace/typeLibrary.ts` holds
`fileTypeLoader` (rejects id/district mismatches and ids in several
districts), `mapTypeLoader` for tests and `resolveTypeList`;
`validateBlockFace` and `houseIntents` take the loader; duplicate ids in
any mix are a validation error; `compile.ts` and `compile-recipes.ts`
pass the loader and fold the resolved library content into
`sources.faces`/`sources.types` so a library edit invalidates the faces
that use it. De Clercqstraat's three types moved to
`types/oud-west/` and the face references them; its chunk, manifest entry
and report hash identically before and after; all 21 faces' resolved
house intents hash identically; fit-golden 140 identical. The tile golden
test (`tileBuildings/golden.test.ts`) was already red before this lane:
an extra `large` pand `0363100012236799` in the Bilderdijkstraat pilot
tiles. **Sculpture reconstruction prototype**
(`lane/sculpture-prototype-20261014`, plan Part 4;
`docs/sculpture-reconstruction-20261014.md`, `scripts/sculptures/`): the
city's 2025 mobile-mapping cloud is catalogued (19–30 M points per tile
near each statue) but its file host `files.lidar.data.amsterdam.nl` does
not resolve (contact datateam.geo@amsterdam.nl); the PDOK 2025 8 cm
surface model is top-down only (Gandhi a 1 m mound, Thijssen a 10.7 m
column of lime canopy, De Dokwerker a 3.4 m post) and is useful only for
position and height; TripoSR (MIT) on the M4 Pro with MPS and scikit-image
marching cubes gives a recognisable real-height ~6k-tri figure in ~20 s
from one licensed Commons photo (De Dokwerker: Rietman CC BY-SA 4.0,
stance and chin right, back invented but plausible; Gandhi: Antony Antony
CC BY 2.0, pose, shawl and book right, staff a stub, plinth half height,
2007 flowers baked on; Theo Thijssen: Alf van Beem PD, block and desk
right, man and boy fused). Strips kit vs A vs B on the demo page.
Recommendation: route B for the ~18 single figures on plinths and for
organic abstract forms, per-figure route B placed on a kit plinth for the
~6 groups, kit primitives for the ~13 slab and lettered memorials;
Hunyuan3D-2 excluded (licence bars EU use), TRELLIS and InstantMesh need
CUDA. Open before any install: bronze tint vs vertex colour, whether
Dutch freedom of panorama covers a 3D model of a copyrighted sculpture
(the user's call), near vs far range. **motorkade-1**: the Tropenmuseum
merge dropped its entry from `signature-landmarks.json` (the lane rebuilt
the manifest from a branch that predated the model), so
`modelAssetVersions.json` lost its fingerprint and `check:manual-landmarks`
failed on main; rebuilt with `--only=motorkade-1`.

picks through a grid per chunk (`prismPick.ts`), 0.38 → 0.03 ms per pick;
(4) MapLibre zoom hold under 1e-6 (the ~1e-8 per-frame jitter fired
`zoom` and a full style re-evaluation on 180 of 180 frames, now 3) plus
the highlight casing hidden until an accent target exists (it drew every
outline on every tile at opacity 0), 3.16 → 2.75 chase; (5) legacy

## 3DBAG shell repair (2026-10-14, night)

Lane `domain/shell-repair-20261014`. `shellRepair: true` on a large
intent closes a LoD2.2 shell's open edges before fitting (the open-edge
rule is the gate's own): caps on flat loops unless already half covered,
wall strips under an open roof edge down to the next roof or the ground
minus the walls already in that plane, strips up from an open wall top,
seams across vertical slits ≤ 0.6 m, and wall-spike clamping only on
triangles touching an open edge, so sound shells never move. Patches
become wall surfaces numbered from 90000 that `walls.ts --repair` lists
and groups can claim; with the flag on, only truly coplanar walls merge
into a panel (`strictMergeClasses`), which alone fixed Westerdoksdijk 9
and Buiksloterweg 5C. A `shell-repair` gate line reports open edge and
IoU before and after. Seven of the eight open-edge pands repair; four are
installed: Singel 457 (red-brick colonnade run, curved stone corner,
KALVERPASSAGE block; its west gable stays blank because a wall standing
above its roof fails the eaves gate), Hirschpassage 2 (arched portals and
iron balconies per 4.3 m pilaster bay), WG-plein 600, Da Costakade 146.
Gillis van Ledenberchstraat 34 is authored but not installed (1300 m² BAG
overlap with pands 238383/243844 fails `check:osm-under-models`);
Revaleiland 58 is still 0.2 m over the open-edge limit. `footprint:
"bag"` rebuilds the shell from the BAG outline split by roof planes: IoU 1
but 76–1250 m of open edge on real data, so it is not usable yet. The
nine IoU pands are not drift (parking decks, courtyards, podium pands
under neighbouring towers, buildings newer than the lidar, the
Museumplein garage): the IoU gate is the wrong test for them and they
stay dropped. New scripts `shell-survey.ts`, `shell-debug.ts`,
`shell-footprint.ts`; twelve synthetic-shell unit tests. Houses without
either flag are byte-identical.

## Stale-install check made exact (2026-10-14, night)

`install-large.ts` now records `meshHash` (the golden's compiled-mesh hash,
shared through `scripts/building-recipes/mesh-hash.ts`) on each catalogue
entry, and `stale-installs.ts` compares that with the golden; the git
heuristic (newest golden commit reachable from the GLB's commit, ancestry
rather than global log order) stays as the fallback for entries without
it. The old global-order heuristic reported 37 false stales right after
the re-install merge because batch 5 branched before the layered default
and its goldens sorted as "newer". All 77 current installs were backfilled
with their golden hash; the seven the ancestry check still flagged were
re-installed (five whose golden was recorded after the install, and the
two byte-identical ones). `npm run check:stale-installs` (`--strict`) is in
`check:canal`.

## layeredKit is the default; parts follow leaning and bent walls (2026-10-14, night)

Lane `domain/layered-default-20261014`. `largeCompile`, `fitLarge` and
the validator treat a missing `layeredKit` as on; `false` keeps the
legacy kit, set on four houses the layered kit pushes over 12k tris
(OBA Javaplein 12.7k, OBA Olympisch Kwartier 12.5k, Politie West
Overtoomsesluis 12.3k, Stadsdeel Nieuw-West 13.4k). The band residue
the re-installs left was not component against component: on Berlage,
Montessori and Stadsloket West the parts fought the 3DBAG wall itself,
which leans (0–9.5 cm over 8.6 m; 5.3 cm) or bends (26 cm over the 65 m
front) off the panel's reference plane; only the Amsterdams Lyceum's 3 cm
gateway rings and 1.2 cm wall lettering were in the tight band. Fixes in
layered mode: `wallProfileOf` in `compose.ts` lays every part off the
wall's actual plan profile when member vertices agree per column within
5 mm and reach ≥ 1.5 cm off the plane; boxes and bands split at bends
over 1 cm (`kinksIn`, Douglas-Peucker); a box laid on that profile drops
its back face; a bent member is emitted per facet (`emitFacets`: earcut
per slab between bends, trapezoids where an opening straddles a bend);
arch rings thinner than 4.5 cm are lifted to 4.5 cm; `drawLettering`
draws closed strokes 4.5 cm off the surface (five times the triangles:
Amsterdams Lyceum +1,424). New ground `mesh-plinth` for a layered curtain
wall (closed dark panel 9 cm off the glass skin over the ground storey;
at 4.5 cm it showed 259 m² of near band, at 9 cm 10.5 m²); Stadsloket
West uses it. Entrepotdok's hoist doors are back on every third bay (11
axes) with a cheaper two-leaf door and 4-segment arched heads: 11,767
tris at 0 m². The default flip plus the profile fix change 52 compiled
meshes (golden re-recorded; e.g. Politie Van Leijenberghlaan 21.2 → 0 m²,
Overtoom 283 18.8 → 0, Nieuwpoortstraat 13.8 → 0, Amstel 142 10.7 → 0),
15 stay byte-identical; only Berlage, Montessori, Amsterdams Lyceum,
Stadsloket West and Entrepotdok were re-installed, so 47 installed GLBs
still carry the old geometry until re-installed. Seven new
`largeTier.test.ts` cases (leaning wall, sill vs reveal, curtain grid on
a bent member, mesh plinth, 3 cm arch ring, lettering, the default).

## The black blocks under the shared frame were a depth-range bug (2026-10-14, night)

Lane `look/shadow-fill-20261014`. MapLibre draws its 3D custom layer with
`gl.depthRange(0, k)` (k = 0.968 measured in the game). Depth range is GL
state, not framebuffer state, so three's shadow pass into its own
framebuffer inherited it: every depth in the shadow map was scaled by k
while receivers compared against the unscaled light depth, and a surface
met a phantom occluder (1−k)·z nearer the sun, ~10 m in the middle of
the 600 m box. Sun-facing walls shadowed themselves: 95 % of the Royal
Palace's pixels and 64 % of the Nassaukade 318 chunk, 45 % of all
building pixels at the Dam; CPU rays toward the sun found an occluder for
only 1–8 % of them, which is how the lane proved it. Bias, map size and
`shadowSide` changed nothing; the model's own `castShadow` off cleared it.
`fullDepthRangeForShadowMap` in `sharedFrame.ts` draws the shadow map at
[0, 1] and restores MapLibre's range for the main pass
(`renderer.shadowMap.fullDepthRange = false` for before/after). After the
fix 96 % of the chunk's remaining shadowed pixels have a real occluder
(its own gables and dormers). `SHADOW_FILL = 0.5` (`shadowIntensity`):
cast shadow keeps half the sun; the reference brick #9a5240 in cast
shadow reads ≥ 70 luma in all six pipelines, lit walls unchanged within 1.
Near-black pixels: Nassaukade 52 % → 6.6 %, Palace 29 % → 0.1 %. Ride
perf: map render median 2.8 → 2.7 ms, all landmarks resident 6.4 → 3.8.
`tests/e2e/shadow-fill.spec.ts` (four spots, both looks, three
configurations) and a "shadow fill" case in `building-look.spec.ts`;
`docs/LOOK.md` §Light has the rule and tables. Side finding: the Palace
gets worse with normal bias ≥ 0.5, which hints at inward-facing normals
in that GLB.

## Street-survey chunks retired; why the block was black (2026-10-14, night)

Lane `buildings/street-survey-retire-20261013` (user, Singelgracht shot:
the Nassaukade 318 block-face chunk near-black beside normal extrusions;
"should we drop all the street survey models… probably?"). Decision: yes.
`streetSurveyMode` in `ordinaryChunks.ts` is `retired` by default
(`?streetChunks=1` loads the 22 chunks, `=0` the 19 per-house models);
nothing loads, so nothing suppresses those pands and they draw as the
generic city. `street-surveys.html` shows the retired state; the face
intents stay as recipe-tile input. The cause of the black: no light-aim
or placement bug (normals, determinant +1.003, sun direction and
`matrixWorld` all check out). Under the default unlit baked shade the chunk
is darker than its neighbours (luma 99 vs 134, 4 % near-black) from its
dark photo-measured tints, glass and slate; under the shared frame (which
`?recipeTiles=1`, `?ownGround=1` and `?sculptures=1` all force) it
self-shadows under the Lambert material and the dark tints are lit by sky
only: 50–59 % of its pixels under luma 60 (5.5 % with shadow casting off).
The Royal Palace shows the same (36 % near-black in shadow), so this is a
shadow-fill level for the look lane, not a per-model fix; the CPU ray
casts find fewer occluders than the screen shows, unexplained. Recipe
tiles stay behind the flag: they exist only inside the shared frame, which
is off by default, and the pilot has no tiles for Nassaukade or De
Clercqstraat; ride perf is within noise in every mode.

## Desktop ride profiled by owner; three fixes (2026-10-14, night)

Lane `perf/desktop-ride-20261013` (user: "there's still perf work to do").
`scripts/ride-perf-owners.mjs` reports ms per frame by owner (self time),
GL work, long frames with their owners and GC, frames uncapped so an
interval is the frame's cost. Chase ride on the fixed route, 1440×900:
median 5.3 → 3.4 ms, p95 7.2 → 5.0. Every frame over 33 ms in every
configuration was a label plan running its 40 occlusion picks at once
(landmark ray picks ~20 ms against every visible mesh, city picks ~7 ms,
the plan ~7 ms; 47 such frames per 12 s on the aerial hold). Fixes: the
label overlay stops deep-copying the MapLibre style every frame
(`styleReady()`; 1.18 → 0.09 ms), occlusion picks run a few per frame
within a 3 ms budget against the current camera (aerial frames over 33 ms
49 → 2, p99 42 → 16 ms; verdicts and label counts identical), and the
signature landmarks cache the view bounds until the camera moves
(`getBounds()` ran per model per frame; 0.48 → 0.16 ms). `ride-perf.spec`
pins the desktop budget (map render median ≤ 6 ms, label overlay mean
≤ 0.6 ms, ≤ 2 frames over 100 ms). `docs/performance/desktop-20261013.md`
has the table per flag: own ground adds ~0.6 ms of three.js, 50 draw
calls and 0.9 M drawn triangles; the shared frame redraws shadows 27 times
in 12 s. Remaining: the HUD street-name pass walks 28,931 anchors per
frame (0.4–1.3 ms; a grid index was no faster), landmark ray picks need a
bounds pre-test, static landmark scenes update matrices per frame, the
bike is drawn twice (0.4 ms); the iPhone profile is still pending.

## Map Recall quiz: wave 2, the review's longlist (2026-10-13)

Three lanes off main 4c46645d, merged on `map-recall/integrate-w2-20261013`.

- **New question forms** (`questionPlan.ts`, `relationQuestions.ts`,
  `bonusPin.ts`, `dailyFive.ts`, each with node tests). *Chains:* the
  selected list is re-ordered greedily toward a next question in the same
  neighbourhood, inside the same area or within 700 m, keeping due reviews
  first and the water syllabus order, with at most three in a row from one
  neighbourhood; on by default, `chain=off` turns it off; the Next button
  says "Next · nearby" only after the reveal. *Relation questions:* an
  obscure street (prominence < 20 or under 400 m) asks "Which is further
  north: Chris Lebeaustraat or Willem van Konijnenburgstraat?" against the
  nearest distractor 250 m clear on an axis (64 of 177 obscure Amsterdam
  streets; distractors are mostly crossing streets, median 85 m apart),
  else "Which of these is in <buurt>?", else the four names. Both candidates
  are drawn in the target's colours before the answer and named after; a
  right answer scores 5,000 and is rated like any Guess Name round.
  *Bonus pin:* after the reveal, "Bonus · where is the Westermoskee?" asks
  for an area's own notable place or the most famous landmark or square
  within 600 m that the hints and clue labels did not already name (parks
  are excluded because the label tiles print park names); one tap, 500
  points within 40 m falling to 0 at 800 m, counted in the total, never a
  review record. *Daily five:* five mixed places near the shared home or
  the centre, seeded by the Europe/Amsterdam day, with a streak in
  `mapRecall.daily.v1` ("Streak 4", "Done today · streak 4"). *Seen-before
  chip:* "Seen 3 days ago · missed before" / "known · 2 reviews" on every
  question card, from `ReviewState`; time and record only, never position.
- **Docked card on wide screens** (`[data-quiz-dock]`, ≥1100 px): a 26 rem
  right column, paper at 92% with a hairline edge and its own scroll; the
  zoom and locate controls move left of it; MapComponent pads fits on the
  right by the dock width (question, reveal, resize) when the holder hugs
  the map's right edge. In the dock the Pinpoint instruction row stacks
  and Guess Name options are one column so names never truncate; the
  folded neighbourhood answer shows the full postcard at dock width with
  "Save postcard" (`PostcardExport`, also in the rack popover). A warm
  tint on the tile pane (`sepia .14 saturate .92 brightness 1.01`) makes
  the CARTO basemap read as part of the paper; labels and markers stay
  crisp. Amsterdam minZoom 12 → 10 so a 10 km waterway fits above the
  phone question card (Amstel checked). The "label above card" e2e now
  measures `.area-plaque` for areas, and the two tests that timed out under
  load wait for the place labels to settle.

  Amsterdam water extract gave Singel the canal plus four pieces of a
  different Singel near Weesp, 18 km away, so the Guess Name fit framed
  both and the canal was a sliver. Pieces are clustered by proximity (1 km

## Home-route start no longer overflows the stack (2026-10-13)

User: the live site crashed with "Maximum call stack size exceeded" after
pressing Start Route (signed in, boat, Home route). `_syncHudLayout` sizes the
plaque by calling `_plaqueNotes`, and on a home ride `_plaqueNotes` asked
`_hudRects().mode` for the home-ring note; before the first layout was cached
that re-entered `_syncHudLayout` forever. The note now reads
`viewport.mode`, which is what the layout's `mode` echoes anyway. Named
regression: `home-destination-varies.spec.ts` "a boat ride from home starts
without a HUD layout stack overflow" (fails on the old bundle).

## Z-fighting found by audit, not by eye (2026-10-13)

User: "is it possible to automatically find instances of texture fighting
in our custom GLBs like this?" (Centraal Station's shed roofs). Yes
(`glb/zfight-audit-20261013`, Opus): `geometryAudit.ts` gains a
coplanar-overlap metric that measures the smaller face's corners against
the larger face's plane and hashes by quantised normal, 2 m cell and
offset, in bands: coplanar (< 2 cm, `zfight-m2`), tight (2–3 cm,
`zfight-tight-m2`, the band that bleeds at distance), near (2–8 cm,
`zfight-near-m2`, informational) and same-material doubled faces. It
labels a patch by its material pair and reports the worst spot, so a
builder fix is a coordinate, not a hunt. Gate: a new export fails above
0.5 m² of coplanar + tight overlap; recorded models may not grow.
`scripts/landmarks/zfight-survey.ts` ranks all 390 models (311 landmarks,
79 ordinary) into `artifacts/zfight-audit/report.md`: 314 have visible
fighting, 286 above the new-export gate; the worst class is "window frame
2 cm proud of an unholed wall" (Vriesseveem 9 11,962 m², HvA Wibautstraat
10,420 m², Kohnstammhuis 6,703 m²). `zfight-validate.ts` renders a model
with MapLibre's projection (near = distance / 75) and measures how much of
the rear face bleeds through; calibration: 2 cm bleeds 9–17 % at 900–1800 m,
3 cm and more not until ~2.7 km. So 3 cm is the minimum clearance; 5 cm is
what the snapper now uses (`snapDetachedParts` rests sheets 5 cm off their
host, was 2.5 cm).

Fixed in this lane: Centraal Station (1,834 → 2.2 m²; the shed arches are a
material split of the roof sheet, gable prisms end inside the outer one,
hip bases face down, north windows un-mirrored), the venue/music/cinema
builders (22 brick-cap-plus-slate-sheet pairs: Studio K 2,297 → 39 m²,
LAB111 574 → 3, OT301 472 → 0.6, OCCII, Cavia, Badhuistheater), RAI (3,694
→ 1.4), De Piramides (710 → 0), Grasweg 116 (1,452 → 0), Stadhuis (328 →
28). Integrator: the baseline merged three ways with batch 3 (disjoint GLB
sets); the 14 batch-3 models were re-baselined under the new metric. The
rest of the ranked list is a board item: the "frame 2 cm proud" class is a
builder-library fix (hole the wall or lift the frame 3 cm), not per-model
work.

## One world-fixed sun and the mood pass (2026-10-13)

User: "sun should be fixed, and the city is dour". Cause of the moving sun
(`look/sun-and-mood-20261013`, Opus): the legacy three.js layers fold the
model placement into the camera, so their lights lived in model space. The
bike's key light turned with the heading (world azimuth 64/208/244/277° at
headings 314/44/134/224°, and it sat below the model), every legacy
landmark's key turned with its placement rotation (9–339° across 71 models
at the Dam), and the streamed city's baked shade came from the north-west
while the shared rig and MapLibre lit from the south-south-west.
`lightRig.ts` now exports `SUN_DIRECTION` (215°/40°), the bake
(`bakedWallShade`, `bakedFaceShade`, `BAKED_SHADE_GLSL`),
`enuDirectionInLocal` and `mapLibreSunPosition`; vehicles, landmarks, trees,
ARTIS animals, the baked city shade and MapLibre's light all re-aim from
them. `tests/e2e/sun-heading.spec.ts` rides four headings beside a
free-standing Nieuw-West slab: each wall seen from two headings within 10 %,
the sun-facing wall brighter, the bike's lit half on the sun's side.

Mood: rig sun `#ffe9cc` 2.15, sky `#e3ebf6` over `#998a72`; baked wall
shade 0.84–1.0 (was 0.8); parity under the rig for mid-grey brick, sun side
102–109, shade 70–75 (LOOK bands 95–110 / 65–75). Flat roofs are three
kinds (`FLAT_ROOF_TONES`: gravel `#9e9281`, membrane `#c3c1bb`, bitumen
`#56585e`) instead of four greys. Own ground (`GROUND_TONES`): lighter warm
pavers, water `#46707c`; the drawn street surfaces keep the roads lane's
`STREET_GROUND` vocabulary and the water stays matte (roughness 0.65, no sun
disc). Foliage: yellow-greens +8° hue, +10 % saturation. Measured in
`tests/e2e/mood-shots.spec.ts` (seven spots, sun and shade sides, luma and

## Map Recall quiz: gameplay and aesthetics pass, wave 1 (2026-10-13)

A play-through review of the quiz surface (desktop and iPhone emulation,
main @ 94e7780f; the write-up with screenshots is the "Map Recall Quiz
Review" artifact) found the reveal, the facts and the postcards each falling
short of the data behind them. Seven lanes in separate worktrees shipped the
shortlist plus two longlist data items; the rest is the wave-2 block in TODO.

- **Area reveal shows the area.** `MapComponent` fills a neighbourhood's
  `areaGeometry` (copper at 0.14 over a dark casing, holes kept) and places
  the plaque at the pole of inaccessibility (`src/mapRecall/polygonLabel.ts`,
  grid cells plus priority queue, tested on a square, a U, a ring and the real
  Grachtengordel), not the bbox centre, which for the horseshoe was the Dam.
  Fits now pad for whichever card is open (`#guess-bottom-card` as well as
  `[data-result-card]`), give features under 1.2 km a 1.2 km frame so a short
  street has water and parks in view, and on wide maps try the open map beside
  the centred card for a closer zoom. A new Pinpoint question fits the search
  boundary, never the feature. Found on the way: Leaflet drops a zoom requested
  during a zoom animation, which is why the re-fit when the card grew was often
  lost and an iPhone reveal sometimes stayed at the city view; fits now wait for
  the running animation. The game-over map gives each round its own hue
  (`roundPalette.ts`, 8 hues at ≥3:1 on CARTO paper), a numbered plaque at the
  pole/midpoint, dashed lines for misses, and folds overlapping names to
  their number.
- **Hints cost, labels teach.** `hintCost.ts`: the round ceiling is 5,000 /
  4,000 / 3,000 / 2,000 for 0–3 revealed hints; the Hint button says what the
  round is still worth; `rateRound` clamps a hinted round to "good" and two
  hints to "hard", so a hinted bullseye no longer schedules as "easy". Tier
  labels are distance-anchored ("Within 60 m", "Within a block", "A few
  streets off", "Right neighbourhood", "Nearby", "Wrong part of town"); the
  old arcade copy truncated on phones. The reveal names the answer once (the
  subtitle: "Spuistraat · off by 109 m"); Guess Name shows "In <neighbourhood>"
  for non-area features.
- **Answer card uses the fact store.** The fold is the first sentence of the
  name origin, two lines (`answerText.ts` sentence split keeps St./ca./lit.,
  initials and patronymics). Expanded: Name → story/local line → "Where it is"
  (district · quarter · landmark relation from the locate hints, which were the
  most useful facts and only showed on request) → every reviewed fact with its
  kind chip → the lede (no longer suppressed by facts) → History → Around here
  → credits last. Register prose without a subject gets one ("Jan Veth:
  Painter and draughtsman…", 826 of 5,333 entries; connective openings such as
  "After…" are left alone). Around here ranks landmarks, schools, churches,
  parks and culture first and allows one shop/food/bike place. Water extracts
  carried `wikipediaExtractSource: "translated"` as a string, which emptied the
  lede's source link; ignored unless an object.
- **Postcards at a size that reads.** On phones the fold shows a 44 px
  "Greetings from X" strip (Pacifico and Anton over the first photo at 25%)
  that opens the full card; on desktop the fold shows the card up to 520 px
  when the card is ≥480 px wide and the window ≥800 px tall, otherwise the
  strip (the review's 1352×761 viewport gets the strip: the result header plus
  MapComponent's 60% padding cap leave no room). The caption is "ZUID ·
  AMSTERDAM" when the stadsdeel is known and fits. Compositor round 5
  (`LARGE_LETTER_CRAFT.md`): one photograph spans a run of 2–4 letters (3–5
  photographs a card, `windowsPerPhoto: 'run'`; `'letter'` keeps the old
  card), a measured per-photo tone skips the posterise step for brick-heavy,
  busy or already-saturated photographs (13 of 32 sample Commons photos go
  soft), and two-line names keep ≥0.62 of a one-line face. `PostcardExport`
  renders a 1280×800 PNG (Commons sends CORS headers, so photos draw clean).
- **The learning loop is visible, and postcards are collected.**
  `progress.ts` (due/known counts, session groups, earned areas) feeds a start
  rail line ("Due today 3 · Known 12"), a `PostcardRack` of earned neighbourhood
  postcards (an area is earned when any mode's state has repetitions ≥1; a
  lapse in every mode loses it; rail strip on phones, a panel over the vista on
  desktop; cards fill in from the extract lazily) with a full-size popover, and
  an end screen titled "Session complete" that leads with the session's best new
  postcard and groups answers Known / Still shaky / New with the next review
  day. The floating "Review guesses on map" pill moved into the button row.
- **Neighbourhood text is cleaned at build.** `scripts/clean-neighborhood-text.ts`
  (`npm run check:neighborhood-text`) drops resident-count and area/density
  sentences from ledes and histories (never the first sentence), fixes the
  stripped-IPA "(, lit." artefact, and turns "Schinkel (waterway here): …"
  prefixes into `borrowedFrom = "Schinkel (waterway)"` on 91 histories and 57
  descriptions across the four cities; the card heads those "History of the
  Schinkel, which runs through here" / "About the Orgelpark, which is here".
  The crime and planning rules of the local-fact policy are deliberately not
  applied to prose: they deleted Weesperbuurt's "Many of its residents were
  deported and murdered."
- **Every Amsterdam area has a story.** `scripts/build-neighborhood-stories.ts`
  replaces the ad-hoc import script; `scripts/data/neighborhood-stories-picks.json`
  holds 61 areas of reviewed picks, each resolved to a verbatim quote in a
  sourced record (neighborhood-history fields, approved area-fact cites, or a
  facts.json `sourceQuote` for a landmark inside the polygon) and refused when
  the quote, a number or the landmark's position fails. Coverage 17 → 78 areas,
  34 → 154 top and 24 → 222 rotating facts; Dutch originals are quoted so edits
  to the English do not break the gate.
- **Checks.** `npm run check:map-recall` (lint, Map Recall unit tests, trivia,
  postcard, neighbourhood text and story checks). Playwright
  `map-recall-trivia`, `map-recall-phone-chrome` and `card-gallery`: 28 passed,
  2 skipped on the merged branch; `build-storybook` clean. The postcard e2e
  count is now ≥3 windows (one per run).

## Hosting: deploys failing on the storage quota again (2026-10-13)

Every "Deploy to Firebase Hosting" run since 14:27 (the push after 922de98,
which is what the live site still serves) fails with HTTP 429 "exceeded the
Hosting storage quota", the 2026-10-01 failure again. Listed through the
Hosting API: 100+ stored versions per site, 17.8 GB on canalrecall and
7.9 GB on edumap, although both sites have `maxVersions: 3`: expired
versions are not collected promptly and the ~40 deploys a day (every push
to main, ~190 + ~100 MB each) outrun it. `scripts/hosting/prune-versions.mjs`
(`npm run hosting:prune`, dry run unless `--apply`) keeps the live release
and the newest three per site and deletes the rest; the manual workflow
`prune-hosting.yml` runs it with the CI service account. The integrator's
own prune was stopped by the session's permission policy (mass delete), so
the prune is the user's call; after it, re-run the newest failed deploy.
The deploy workflow now skips pushes that only touch `docs/**`, `*.md` or
`artifacts/**`.

**Bridges** (`ground/bridges-elevation-20261013`, Opus): humps were already
measured; `clampDeckGrade` puts a 1:8 lower envelope over each deck span
(13 of 931 decks move > 2 cm, no crown lowered > 5 cm) and bridge bands
sample at 0.75 m at LOD 0 so they follow the hump. `measuredDeckTop` fills
the footprint out to the railings (the Westerkerk complaint: water showed
between carriageway, sidewalk and parapet); abutments at every land/water
change down past the water; plinth plus post-and-rail railings every 1.8 m
in Amsterdam green (wood on wooden decks), LOD 0 only; piers in ~8 m bays
where the water span exceeds 12 m, one vault per bay on masonry arches;

(a first version fenced the road at Raampoort); the 110 movable footprints
get a shared counterweight-frame unit (two over 24 m). Eight bridges pinned

probe, railings both sides, abutments ≥ 2, pier rule): Westerkerk BRU0063

Brug's two units read as one gantry, no slope physics in `game.js`
(suggested: `speed -= 9.81·sin(pitch)·0.35·dt` from `riderPose().pitch`).

## A stopped boat turns on the spot promptly (2026-10-13)

User: "boat needs to be able to do a stopped turn when up against a wall
faster, it's annoying when it gets stuck". With no way on, boat steering was
floored at 0.28 of its turn rate (~0.48 rad/s, ~6.5 s for a half-turn), and
nosed into a quay the boat has no way on: the quay guard rolls position back
every frame but never heading, so the standstill floor was the whole story.
`BOAT_MIN_STEER_FACTOR` (constants.js) is now 0.8, ~1.37 rad/s and a ~2.3 s
half-turn. It only changes behaviour below 16 px/s, where the speed factor
ramps to full, so handling under way is unchanged. Pinned by
`tests/e2e/boat-stopped-turn.spec.ts` (one second of full lock at rest must
turn more than 1.2 rad; the old floor gave ~0.48).

## Bespoke landmark process: photo-first brief, signature inventory gate; six ornament retro-fits (2026-10-13)

User 2026-10-13, after the Hoofdbureau shipped without its Amsterdam-arms
relief: "fix your custom landmark process so it would have been right the
first time". Root cause was the integrator's brief (written from memory:
"corner tower, carved portal", both wrong) and a checklist that only knew
windows and holes; the stock tools also skipped the wall — `all-walls
--min-len=14` and `review-sheet --walls=6` both drop the 13.9 m Marnixstraat
end wall that carries the relief. Lane `landmarks/ornament-inventory-20261013`
(Opus): `scripts/landmarks/landmark-brief.ts --pand=<id> --id=<slug>` takes
every exposed wall ≥ 4 m (up to 30), saves a rectified crop, a second year
and an aimed thumbnail per wall, collects BAG/3DBAG/monument-register facts,
quotes Wikipedia sections on sculpture and facade (the new Hoofdbureau brief
quotes nl.wikipedia "Elandsgracht 117" § Beeldhouwwerken: the arms with
imperial crown and two lions, the Van Moerkerken verse on the banner, the
three Hildo Krop figures, architects Van der Wilk and Messer) and writes
`<id>-brief.md` plus a skeleton `<id>-inventory.json`. Schema
`src/canalRecall/landmarks/ornamentInventory.ts` (items with plan modelled /
simplified / skipped-with-reason / open; excuse skips such as "cannot
express" refused). Gate `landmark-inventory-gate.ts`: a landmark first
exported after 2026-10-14 (git history) or never committed must have an
inventory with no open items, no `needs-modeller` skips, every photographed
wall checked and every signature item modelled or simplified;
`build-manual-landmarks.ts` refuses the export (`LANDMARK_INVENTORY_GATE=warn`
downgrades), `audit:glb` adds `signature-inventory`, `check-landmark-inventory.ts`
is in `check:canal`, `review-sheet.ts --inventory` adds a photo-crop /
render-crop column per item. The Hoofdbureau (exported 2026-10-13) is not
gated; its inventory has 29 items (9 modelled, 3 simplified, 1 skipped, 16
open) and the inventory column caught a second defect: the end wall is
misregistered (arms a storey higher and larger in the photo; the model wraps
ribbon windows round the blank left 5 m). Survey of 60 landmarks
(`ornament-inventory.json`, `ornament-inventory.ts --strip`): 93 items, 21
open, ranked in the board. Retro-fits (≤ 1.5k tris each, `audit:glb` PASS,
strips panorama | before | after): museum-amsterdam-noord name boards
GEMEENTE BADHUIS / MUSEUM AMSTERDAM NOORD (1,792 → 2,410 tris), nassaukerk
NASSAUKERK raised letters on the blank band (6,751 → 7,269), vondelkerk hands
on the four clock faces (14,369 → 14,465), de-school LTS letters over the
porch, american-hotel AMERICAN on the canopy and striped awnings over the
café arches (35,806 → 36,414), willem-de-zwijgerkerk green name plate.
Shared helper `scripts/landmarks/ornament-kit.ts` (`raisedLettering`,
`clockHands`). Integrator: manifests and lod1 regenerated; the first
re-export of vondelkerk in a six-id process failed the audit (see board,
export determinism), a single-id export is deterministic and passes.

## Hoofdbureau van Politie: ribbon fronts and the corner relief (2026-10-13)

User report with a photo of the Marnixstraat/Elandsgracht corner: the model had
key features missing. Three fronts used `brick-bay-grid` (tall punched windows)
even though the intent's own notes and the panoramas showed white steel-window
ribbons:
- the north-west wall (group 0);
- the 45 m Marnixstraat front of the north wing (group 3);
- the low bridge wing on the Singelgracht (group 5, formerly 4).

All three are `ribbon-windows` now. The north end wall of the Marnixstraat wing
(3DBAG wall 190) is its own blank group. `addEndWallRelief` in the builder draws
that wall by hand, from panorama `recording_2025-07-03_10-58-37_00361` and the
user photo:
- the ribbons wrapping round from the long front;
- the Amsterdam arms relief: crowned shield with three saltires on a pale, two
  rampant lions, a long banner;
- three figures on brackets;
- six round windows;
- the open ground storey behind white columns.

Inserting the group shifted the indices after it, and the intent notes were
renumbered to match. Lesson: the per-wall review sheet (`review-sheet.ts`)
already showed punched windows against ribbons on three walls; read its overlays
before a large-tier landmark ships. The open-edge gate in
`hoofdbureau-elandsgracht-check.ts` was already failing on `main` (108 edges,
9.8 m) and is unchanged.

## "See it in the game" opens the ride instead of the menu (2026-10-13)

User report: the What's New links did nothing visible. The `#race=` share link
loaded the ride, but `_checkShareLink` never closed route setup, so the ride sat
hidden behind the setup rail and its hero photo. (The review scripts had been
calling `setSetupOpen(false)` themselves, which hid the problem.) Share links now
close setup the way a launch from setup does. The links on What's New and Street
chunks now add `?travel=car`, so they open the street ride: a boat can't reach most
buildings. `travel=car|boat` is applied to the saved preferences the same way the
F3 ferry preview link does it. Checked on the Waag link: the rider spawns about
30 m from the anchor, with the model in view.

## Gameplay follow-ups: review-ride planner, exposure scheduling, questions-a-minute setting, finish-card story, ferry prompts (2026-10-13)

Lane `gameplay/followups-20261013` (Sonnet), merged with the `game.js` ferry
branch and the `index.html` style block added by the integrator.

**Review-ride planner, two independent bugs.** (1) `pickReviewRoute` treats a
due name within 0.2 km of the landmark line as "covered" and only uncovered
names get a via; Avenhornstraat sits within 0.2 km of the line to Kazerne
Zebra, so every pick was "covered" with no via and no runner-up, and
`game-route.js` only plans when there are alternatives, a via or a stop. The
chosen pair is now also offered as runner-ups with each grazed name as a via
(`REVIEW_MISSED_VIA_TRIES = 2`), dropped when the direct ride already passes
every name; `_reviewRoute` is replaced when the via name changes. (2)
`planLearningRoadRoute` rejected any via path with a repeated position; two
graph nodes can share a position (a bridge ramp meeting its deck), so every
stretch of Avenhornstraat failed whatever the via. Consecutive equal
positions now count once in `roadGraph.ts`; turn-back, lollipop and dead-end
rejections unchanged. The spec seeds `Math.random` (mulberry32) so the origin
is stable; no assertion weakened; `check-play-delight.ts` allows a runner-up
that is the pick's own pair with a via.

**Exposure.** `RecallStore.expose()` (`recallExposure.ts`) parks a shown-but-
not-asked name: 30 min first, doubling per repeat, capped at a day; not a
review event; `ReviewState` gained optional `exposures`/`lastExposedAt`;
`buildKnowledgeReview` skips exposure-only states. `answerPath.ts` already
called it.

**Setting.** `maxAsksPerMinute` 1/2/3/0, default 2, persisted; hidden
`<select id="max-asks-per-minute">` plus a "Questions a minute" strip row in
`OverlayApp.tsx`; Storybook `AdvancedOptionsQuestionsOffPhone`; e2e checks
the choice reaches the budget and survives a reload.

**Finish-card ghost was the story, not the runtime**: the finish story drew
`_renderFinish()` twice (once at mount, again when the photo loaded) on a
canvas it never cleared, so the translucent plaque showed the first draw
through, and on desktop the scrim was applied twice (old desktop baselines
were darker than the game). The story now repaints the map before each draw;
five baselines re-recorded (`finish-card`, `-calm-mode`, `-bike`, `-transit`,
`portrait-finish-card`).

**Styles and ferry.** `ridingPromptStyleBlock()` emits the exact
`<style id="canal-riding-prompt-styles">` pasted into `index.html`, with the
runtime injection kept as a fallback and a drift test. `_updateQuizOnFerry`
ticks the feedback timeout and an open riding prompt on ferry frames
(`ferryPrompt.test.ts`); `game.js` calls it in the ferry branch of
`_updateRacing`.

Checks: lint, 42 game unit tests, answer-path, bottom-HUD (160 + 384
scenarios), route-selection, road-graph, preferences, play-delight,
road-name-heading, Storybook build, `riding-pacing`/`review-ride`/
`storybook-visual` e2e (54): all pass.

(`src/canalRecall/buildingRecipe/fitLarge.ts`) builds per-wall panels from the
3DBAG LoD2.2 walls (coplanar walls in different wall groups stay separate via

## De Waag roof rebuilt from the measured 3DBAG planes (2026-10-13)

User report: the Waag gallery card showed one long 22.5 m hip over the whole
block, turret cones buried in it, a flat dormer box sticking out of the hip, and a
see-through gap beside the front turret. The 3DBAG roof planes and the four
municipal panoramas show four parts instead, now drawn as clean slate planes in
`scripts/landmarks/waag-builder.ts`:
- front (weigh-house) block: a truncated hip with eaves at 10.4 and a flat top at
  16.7, with finials on the top corners;
- rear (gate) block: a hip with gentle sides and a steep NNW end, ridge 16.8;
- a 13.1 deck between the big towers;
- a tall octagonal central spire with its apex at 25.6.

The big towers get octagonal roofs up to the 3DBAG apex at 20.0. The five dormers
are set into their slopes, so their caps end inside the roof. Raw 3DBAG roof
planes were tried first and rendered as broken shards with holes, which is why
the roofs are authored. Known leftover: the stone bands on the rear turrets and
the ENE big tower stick out as crescents because the shell's towers are not
circular.

## Own ground: per-polder water, BGT widths per way, 202 more measured bridges (2026-10-13)

the three data blockers for own-ground default-on. **Water levels**: AGV/Waternet
"Peilgebieden Vigerend" (DAMO register, ArcGIS FeatureServer; the Rijkswaterstaat
national WFS has geometry but null levels for Amsterdam) → `elevation-v1/water-levels.json`
(+10 KB gz), NAP level per water polygon and shore (majority peilgebied; fixed
levels as is, seasonal/flexible at the band midpoint; 705/707 parsed; 5,818 of
12,777 polygons and 45% of shores joined, open water stays −0.40 m NAP).

`GameGround.waterLevelAt`; integrator wired the boat and ferry to

water −3.47 (VP −2.17 m NAP); Herengracht cell uniformly −1.77. **Widths**: BGT
`wegdeel` (PDOK OGC API, CC0, 1,164 tiles cached) sampled by cross-lines at
25/50/75% of each way, own surface run within 2.5 m, footpath and cycle path
summed per side, median over stations; dual carriageways measure to the near
edge twice; bridge ways prefer `relatieve_hoogteligging ≥ 1`. 71,703 of 97,372
drawable ways (73.6%) get `OsmWay.bw = [width, sidewalk, cycle]` in decimetres
(+0.44 MB gz over the cells); `crossSection` prefers it, subtracting painted
cycle lanes; `bgt-width-by-class.json` (median/p10/p90 per OSM class) for the
2D physics reader, not yet wired. Where OSM `width` tags exist BGT differs by
0.8 m (cycleway) to 3.7 m (secondary) on average. **Bridges**: the
`feat/measured-bridges` AHN method on the 891 fallback footprints
(`scripts/elevation/build-bridge-surfaces-v2.ts`, extractor `--extra-profiles`;
cells byte-identical, only `bridges.json` changed, +79 KB gz): 202 non-movable
decks measured (129 humped over 0.3 m, max 1.82 m; 113 concrete, 44 wooden,
40 steel, 5 masonry arch) → 931 measured, 689 fallback. 39 movable bridges were
measurable but are kept flat by design. Not measured: 127 without an OSM road
through the footprint, 111 under 2 m wide, 100 viaduct-like, 29 over 65 m, 128
AHN gaps, 25 unnumbered rows. Checks: own-ground 33, elevation 11, 294 cells
fully measured, own-ground-game e2e 8/8 (lane) and 4/4 desktop (integrator),
lint. Raw inputs archived to `map-recall2-source-data/datasets/own-ground-20261013/`.
